bartholomaios.notes: Βαρθολομαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Aram. בַּר־תָּלְמַי, son of Tolmai), Bartholomew, the Apostle (see: Ναθαναήλ): Mat.10:3, Mrk.3:18, Luk.6:14, Act.1:13.† (AS)

bartimaios.notes: Βαρτίμαιος, -ου, ὁ (-μαῖος, T; perh. Aram. בַּר־טִמְאַי, see DB, iv, p. 762), Bartimæus: Mrk.10:46.† (AS)

barus.notes: βαρύς, -εῖα, ύ, [in LXX chiefly for כָּבֵד ;] heavy: Mat.23:4. Metaphorical, burdensome: ἐντολή, 1Jn.5:3; severe (perh. impressive): ἐπιστολή, 2Co.10:10; weighty: τὰ βαρύτερα τ. νόμου, Mat.23:23; αἰτιώματα, Act.25:7;…

barutimos.notes: βαρύτιμος, -ον (βαρύς, τιμή), of great value, very costly: Mat.26:7 (T, πολυτίμου) .† (AS)

basanismos.notes: βασανισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (βασανίζω), [in LXX: 4Ma.9:6 11:2 * ;] torture, torment: Rev.9:5 14:11 18:7, 10, 15.† (AS)

basanistes.notes: βασανιστής, -οῦ, ὁ (βασανίζω), prop., a torturer; used of a gaoler, Mat.18:34.† (AS)

basanizo.notes: βασανίζω (βάσανος), [in LXX: 1Ki.5:3, Sir.4:17, and frequently in Wi, II, 4Mac ;] __1. prop., to rub on the touchstone, put to the test. __2. to examine by torture, hence, generally, to torture, torment, distress:…

basanos.notes: βάσανος, -ου, ὁ (of Oriental origin), [in LXX chiefly for כְּלִמָּה ,אָשָׁם, and frequently in 4Mac ;] __1. prop., touchstone, a dark stone used in testing metals. __2. examination by torture. __3. torment, torture:…

basileia.notes: βασιλεία, -ας, ἡ (βασιλεύω), [in LXX chiefly for מַמְלָכָה ,מַלְכוּת ;] __1. prop. abstract, sovereignty, royal power, dominion: Luk.1:33 22:29, Jhn.18:36, Act.1:6, Heb.1:8, 1Co.15:24; λαβεῖν β., Luk.19:12, 15…

basileios.notes: βασίλειος, -ον (also -α, -ον; βασιλεύς), [in LXX; Exo.19:6, Deu.3:10 (מַמְלָכָה), Exo.23:22, Wis.18:15, 3Ma.3:28, 4Ma.3:8 * ;] royal: 1Pe.2:9 (LXX) (see Hort, in l.).† royal, regal, kingly;, metaphorically possessed…

basileuo.notes: βασιλεύω, (βασιλεύς), [in LXX for מלךְ, its parts and derivatives, exc. 4Ki.15:5 (ישׁב) ;] to be king, to reign, rule: 1Ti.6:15; with genitive (cl.), Mat.2:22; before ἐπί, with accusative (= Heb. מלךְ על; Bl., §36,…

basileus.notes: βασιλεύς, -έως, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for מֶלֶךְ ;] a king: Mat.1:6 2:1; used by courtesy of Herod the Tetrarch, Mat.14:9; of the Roman Emperor, as frequently in κοινή (Deiss., LAE, p. 367), 1Pe.2:13, 17; of the Christ,…

basilikos.notes: βασιλικός, -ή, -όν (βασιλεύς), [in LXX for מֶלֶךְ and its cognates ;] royal, belonging to a king: χώρα, Act 12:20; ἐσθής, Act.12:21; νόμος β., a supreme law, "a law which governs other laws and so has a specially…

basilissa.notes: βασίλισσα, -ης, ἡ (in Attic, βασιλεία, βασιλίς), [in LXX chiefly for מַלְכָּה ;] a queen: Mat.12:42, Luk.11:31, Act.8:27, Rev.18:7.† (AS)

basis.notes: βάσις, ־εως, ἡ (βαίνω), [in LXX chiefly for אֶדֶן ;] __1. a step (Æsch., al.). __2. Hence, a foot (Plat.; Wis.13:18): Act.3:7.† (AS)

baskaino.notes: βασκαίνω, [in LXX: Deu.28:54, 56 (רעע), Sir.14:6, 8*.] __1. to slander (Dem.). __2. to blight by the evil eye, to fascinate, bewitch: Gal.3:1.† (AS)

bastazo.notes: βαστάζω, [in LXX: Jdg.16:30 (נטה), Rut.2:16, 2Ki.23:5, 4Ki.18:14 and Job.21:3 (נשׂא), Sir.6:25, Da TH Bel 36 * ;] __1. to take up with the hands, to lift: λίθους, Jhn.10:31. __2. to bear, to carry, as a burden, and…

bathmos.notes: βαθμός, -οῦ, ὁ, Ion. form of βασμός (βαίνω, to step), [in LXX 1Ki.5:5 (מִפְתָּן), 4Ki.20:9, 10 11 (מַעֲלָה), Sir.6:36 * ;] a step (4Ki, l.with, of degrees of a dial); metaphorically, a degree, standing: 1Ti.3:13.† (AS)

bathos.notes: βάθος, -εος (-ους), τό, [in LXX for מְצוּלָה ,תַּחְתִּי, etc. ;] depth: Mat.13:5, Mrk.4:5, Rom.8:39, Eph.3:18; τὸ β., the deep sea: Luk.5:4; metaphorically, β. πλούτου . . . Θεοῦ, Rom.11:33; τὰ β. τ. Θεοῦ (the Divine…

bathuno.notes: βαθύνω (βαθύς), [in LXX for עמד: Psa.91 (92):5, Jer.29 (49):8 30(49)30 * ;] to deepen: Luk.6:48.† (AS)

bathus.notes: βαθύς (genitive -έως, vernac., Lk, l.with; Bl., §8, 5), -εῖα, -ύ, [in LXX chiefly for עמק ;] deep; Jhn.4:11; metaphorically, ὄρθρου βαθέως (see supr.), early dawn, Luk.24:1; ὕπνος, Act.20:9; τὰ β. τοῦ Σατανᾶ,…

batos.notes: βάτος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ, [in LXX (always masc, as in Attic): Exo.3:2-4, Deu.33:16 (סְנֶה), Job.31:40 (בָּאְשָׁה)* ;] a bramble-bush: Luk.6:44, Act.7:30, 35; ἐπὶ τοῦ (τῆς) β., in the place concerning the bush: Mrk.12:26,…

batrachos.notes: βάτραχος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Ex 8, Psa.77 (78):45 104 (105):30 (צְכַרִדֵּעַ), Wis.19:10 * ;] a frog: Rev.16:13.† (AS)

battologeo.notes: βατταλογέω, -ῶ (Rec. βαττολ-, D, βλαττ- = βατταρίζω, prob. onomatop.; see MM, see word; DCG, ii, 499b, 790a); to stammer, repeat idly: Mat.6:7 (Cremer, 765).† (AS)

bdelugma.notes: βδέλυγμα, -τος, τό (βδελύσσω), [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁקֶץ ,תּוֹעֵבָה ;] an abomination, a detestable thing: Luk.16:15, Rev.17:4, 5 21:27; τὸ β. τ. ἐρημώσεως (Dan LXX 12:11, cf . 1Ma.1:54; DB, i, 12f.; DCG, i, 6f.),…

bdeluktos.notes: βδελυκτός, ή, -όν (βδελύσσω), [in LXX: Pro.17:15 (תּוֹעֵבָה), Sir.41:5, 2Ma.1:27 * ;] abominable, detestable: Tit.1:16 (Cremer, 137).† (AS)

bdelussomai.notes: βδελύσσω, βδελύσσομαι (βδέω, to stink), [in LXX chiefly for שׁקץ ,תּעב ;] in cl., mid. only (Attic, -ττομαι); to make foul; pass., Rev.21:8; mid., to turn away in disgust from, to detest: Rom.2:22 (Cremer, 137).† (AS)

bebaioo.notes: βεβαιόω, -ῶ (βέβαιος), [in LXX: Ps 40 (41)12 (נצב hi.), 118 (119)28 (קוּם pi.), 3Ma.5:42 * ;] to confirm, establish, secure, of things (cl.): λόγον, Mk 16:[20]; ἐπαγγελίας, Rom.15:8; of persons (DCG, ii, 605):…

bebaios.notes: βέβαιος, -ον (also -α, -ον; βαίνω), [in LXX: Est.3:13, Wis.7:23, 3Ma.5:31 7:7, 4Ma.17:4 * ;] firm, secure: ἄγκυρα, Heb.6:19; metaphorically, sure (esp. "in the sense of legally guaranteed security," Deiss., BS, 109;…

bebaiosis.notes: βεβαίωσις, -εως, ἡ (βεβαιόω, which see), [in LXX: Lev.25:23 (צְמִיתֻת), Wis.6:19 * ;] confirmation: τ. εὐαγγελίου, Php.1:7; εἰς β., Heb.6:16, a phrase frequently in π. of guarantee in a business transaction (Deiss.,…

bebeloo.notes: βεβηλόω, -ῶ (βέβηλος), [in LXX chiefly for חלל ;] to profane: τ. σάββατον, Mat.12:5; τ. ἱερόν, Act.24:6 (Cremer, 141).† SYN.: κοινόω, which see (AS)

bebelos.notes: βέβηλος, -ον (βαίνω, whence βηλός, a threshold), [in LXX chiefly for חֹל ;] __1. permitted to be trodden, accessible (see DCG, ii, 422b); hence, __2. (opposite to ἱερός) unhallowed, profane: of things, 1Ti.4:7 6:20,…

beelzeboul.notes: Βεελζεβούλ (WH, App., 159, Rec., βεελζεβούλ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בַּעַל, lord, and the Talmudic זִבּוּל, from זֶבֶל, dung (Dalman, Gr., 137.n), or perh. זִבֻל, habitation, but, see DB, iv, 409f.; DCG, i, 181). The AV,…

belial.notes: Βελίαλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בְּלִיַּעַל, worthlessness, but see DB, i, 268), Belial, a name of Satan: 2Co.6:15, Rec. See next word.† Βελιάρ, ὁ, indecl. (another form of previous word, "due to harsh Syriac…

belos.notes: βέλος, -εος, τό (βάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for חֵץ ;] a missile, a dart: Eph.6:16.† (AS)

beltion.notes: βελτίων, -ον (genitive -ονος), comp. of ἀγαθός, [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב ;] neut. as adv., better, very well: 2Ti.1:18 (also Act.10:28 D). On elative use in these passages, see M, Pr., 78, 236.† (AS)

bema.notes: βῆμα, -τος, τό (βαίνω), [in LXX: Deu.2:5 (מִדְרָךְ), Neh.8:4 (מִגְדָּל), I Est.9:42, Sir.19:30 45:9, 2Ma.13:26 * ;] __1. a step, stride, pace: Act.7:5. __2. a raised place, a platform reached by steps, originally…

beniamin.notes: Βενιαμίν, (Rec. -μίν), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בֶּנְיָמִין), Benjamin: Act.13:21, Rom.11:1, Php.3:5, Rev.7:8.† (AS)

bernike.notes: Βερνίκη (elsewhere Βερενίκη), Macedonian form of Φερενίκη, cf. Veronica, Victoria), -ης, ἡ, Bernice, Berenice, dau. of Herod Agrippa I: Act.25:13, 23 26:3o.† (AS)

beroia.notes: Βέροια, -ας, ἡ, Berœa, a city of Macedonia: Act.17:10, 13.† (AS)

berullos.notes: βήρυλλος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ, [in LXX: Tob.13:17 (-ύλλιον in Exo.28:20, שֹׁהַם * ;]) beryl, a jewel of sea-green colour: Rev.21:20.† (AS)

bethania.notes: Βηθανία, -ας (also -ιά, indecl., Luk.19:29 and in B*, Mrk.11:1), ἡ, (Heb. בֵּית עֲנִיָּה, house of affliction, accusative to Jerome, or perh., house of dates, cf. Bethphage), Bethany; __1. a village fifteen furlongs…

bethesda.notes: Βηθεσδά, ἡ, indecl. (deriv. uncertain, see Westc. on Jhn.5:2, and DB, i, 279), Bethesda, a pool in Jerusalem: Jhn.5:2, Rec. (Βηθζαθά, WH, Βηθσαϊδά, WH, mg.).† (AS)

bethleem.notes: Βηθλέεμ, ἡ, indecl. (Heb. בֵּית לֶחֶם, house of bread), Bethlehem, a town 6 m. S. of Jerusalem: Mat.2:1, 5 6, 8, 16, Luk.2:4, 15 Jhn.7:42.† (AS)

bethphage.notes: Βηθφαγή (L, -γῆ), ἡ, indecl. (Aram. בֵּית־פַּגֵּי, house of unripe figs; Dalman, Gr., 191), Bethphage: Mat.21:1, Mrk.11:1, Luk.19:29.† (AS)

bethsaida.notes: Βηθσαιδά (Rec. -σαϊδά), and -δάν (Mt, Mk, ll. with), ἡ, indecl. (Syr., house of fish), Bethsaida, a town on NE. shore of the Sea of Galilee: Luk.9:10. It is generally supposed that a second B. on the W. shore is…

bia.notes: βία, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX for פֶּרֶךְ, etc. ;] strength, force, violence: Act.5:26 21:35 24:7 27:41.† (AS)

biaios.notes: βίαιος, -α, -ον (βία), [in LXX for אָנַשׁ, עַז, צַר, etc. ;] violent: Act.2:2.† (AS)

biastes.notes: βιαστής, -οῦ, ὁ (βιάζω), late form of βιατάς; __1. strong, forceful. __2. violent (Philo): Mat.11:12 (see: βιάζω).† (AS)

biazo.notes: βιάζω (βία), and depon. -ομαι, [in LXX for פּרץ, פּצר, etc. ;] to force, constrain, rare in active (poet, and late prose), but found in cl. in pass., and so perh. βιάζεται, suffereth violence, Mat.11:12, EV (but see…

biblaridion.notes: βιβλαρίδιον, -ου, τό (diminutive of βιβλάριον, diminutive of βίβλος), a little book: Rev.10:2, 8 (WH, βιβλιόν, T2, 7 βιβλιδάριον) 9, 10. Not hitherto found elsewhere.† (AS)

biblion.notes: βιβλίον, -ου, τό (diminutive of βίβλος, which see), [in LXX also in the alternat. form βυβ-, chiefly for סֶפֶר and the most frequently of the cognate forms ;] __1. a paper, letter, written document: β. ἀποστασίου,…

biblos.notes: βίβλος, -ου, ἡ (variant form of βύβλος, the Egyptian papyrus, paper made from its fibrous coat), [in LXX for סֶפֶר, the form βύβ- being sometimes used ;] a book, a roll, used much less frequently than βιβλίον, and…

bibrosko.notes: βιβρώσκω, poët, and late prose, [in LXX for אכל ;] to eat: Jhn.6:13.† (AS)

bioo.notes: βιόω, -ῶ (βίος), [in LXX: Pro.7:2 9:6 (חיה), Job.29:18, Wis.4:4 א 1, 12:23, Sir.40:28, 4Ma.5:22 17:18 * ;] to spend life, to live: τ. χρόνον βιῶσαι (cl., more frequently 2 aor., -ναι), 1Pe.4:2 (cf. Jb, l.with).†…

bios.notes: βίος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for יָמִים ;] __1. period or course of life, life: Luk.8:14, 1Ti.2:2, 2Ti.2:4, 1Jn.2:16. __2. living, livelihood, means (in Pro.31:14 for לֶחֶם; see DCG, ii, 39a): Mrk.12:44, Luk.8:43…

biosis.notes: βίωσις, -εως, ἡ (βιόω), [in LXX: Si prol. 12 * ;] manner of life: Act.26:4.† (AS)

biotikos.notes: βιωτικός, -ή, -όν (βιός), pertaining to life, hence, worldly (Field, Notes, 171): Luk.21:34, 1Co.6:3, 4.† (AS)

bithunia.notes: Βιθυνία, -ַας, Bithynia, a province in Asia Minor: Act.16:7, 1Pe.1:1.† (AS)

blapto.notes: βλάπτω, [in LXX: Pro.25:20, Tob.12:2, Wis.10:8 18:2, 2Ma.12:22, 4Ma.9:7 * ;] to hurt, injure: with accusative, Mrk.16:[18], Luk.4:35.† (AS)

blasphemeo.notes: βλασφημέω, -ῶ (βλάσφημος), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:4 (יכח hi.) ib. 6, 22 (גּדף pi.), Isa.52:5 (נאץ hith.), Dan LXX 3:29 (96) (אמר שׁלח), Tob.1:18, Da TH Bel 9, 2Ma.2 * ;] __1. to speak lightly or profanely of sacred things…

blasphemia.notes: βλασφημία, -ας, ἡ (βλάσφημος), [in LXX: Eze.35:12 (נֶאָצָה), Da TH 3:29 (96) (שׁלה), Tob.1:18, 1Ma.2:6, 2Ma.8:4 10:35 15:24 * ;] __(a) railing slander: Mat.12:31 15:19, Mrk.3:28 7:22, Eph.4:31, Col.3:8, 1Ti.6:4, Ju…

blasphemos.notes: βλάσφημος, -ον (βλασ-, of uncertain deriv., see Thayer, Boisacq; + φήμη, speech), [in LXX: Isa.66:3 (מְבָרֵךְ אָוֶן), Wis.1:6, Sir.3:16, 2Ma.9:28 10:4, 36 * ;] __(a) evil-speaking, slanderous, blasphemous: Act.6:11,…

blastano.notes: βλαστάνω, [in LXX for צמח, etc. ;] __1. to sprout: Mat.13:26, Mrk.4:27, Heb.9:4. __2. In late Gk., causal, to make to grow, produce: with accusative, Jas.5:18.† (AS)

blastos.notes: Βλάστος, -ου, ὁ, Blastus, chamberlain of Agrippa: Act.12:20.† (AS)

blemma.notes: βλέμμα, -τος, τό (βλέπω), a look, a glance: βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ, 2Pe.2:8, sight and hearing, a sense not found for β. in Gk. lit., but perh. recognized in the vernacular (ICC, in l.)† (AS)

blepo.notes: βλέπω, [in LXX chiefly for ראה, also for פּנה, etc. ;] __1. of bodily sight; __(a) to see, have sight (opposite to τυφλὸς): Mat.12:22, Jhn.9:7, Act.9:9, Rom.11:8, Rev.3:18, al.; __(b) to perceive, look (at), see:…

bleteon.notes: βλητέος, -α, -ον (gerundive of βάλλω), (that which) one must put: Luk.5:38.† (AS)

boanerges.notes: Βοανηργές, indecl. (on the derivation, see Dalman, Gr., 144; Words, 42; Swete, Mk., l.with; DCG, i, 216), Boanerges: Mrk.3:17.† (AS)

boao.notes: βοάω, -ῶ (βοή), [in LXX chiefly for זעק, צעק, קרא ;] __1. absol., to cry, call out: Mat.3:3, 27:46, Mrk.1:3 15:34, Luk.3:4 9:38 18:38, Jhn.1:23, Act.8:7 17:6 25:24, Gal.4:27. __2. C. dative, to call on for help (Heb.…

boe.notes: βοή, -ῆς, ἡ, [in LXX for זְעָקָה, etc. ;] a cry: Jas.5:4.† (AS)

boetheia.notes: βοήθεια, -ας, ἡ (see: βοηθέω), [in LXX for עֵזֶר, etc. ;] help: Heb.4:16; pl., helps, "frapping," a technical nautical term (MM, Exp., x; DB, ext., 367): Act.27:17.† (AS)

boetheo.notes: βοηθέω, -ῶ (βοή + θέω, to run), [in LXX chiefly for עזר ;] to come to aid, to help, succour: absol., Act.21:28; with dative, Mat.15:25, Mrk.9:22, 24 Act.16:9, 2Co.6:2" (LXX), Heb.2:18, Rev.12:16.† (AS)

boethos.notes: βοηθός, -ον (see: βοηθέω), [in LXX chiefly for עזר ;] __1. (poët. -όος), hasting to the war-cry (Hom.). __2. helping, auxiliary; as subst. (Hdt.), a helper: Heb.13:6 (LXX).† (AS)

bole.notes: βολή, -ῆς, ἡ (βάλλω), [in LXX: Gen.21:16 (טחה), 2Ma.5:3, 3Ma.5:26 * ;] a throw; λίθου β. (Thuc., v, 65, 2), a stone's throw: Luk.22:41.† (AS)

bolizo.notes: βολίζω (βολίς, in sense of sounding-lead), to heave the lead, take soundings: Act.27:28.† (AS)

bomos.notes: βωμός, -οῦ, ὁ (βαίνω), [in LXX (Hex.) for מִזְבֵּחַ, in Proph., chiefly for בָּמָה ;] __1. any raised place, a platform. __2. an altar: Act.17:23 (cf. θυσιαστήριον and see DB, i, 75).† (AS)

booz.notes: Βοός and Βοές (RV, Βοάζ, Rec. Βοόζ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בֹּעַז), Boaz (Rut.2:1): Mat.1:5, Luk.3:32.† (AS)

borboros.notes: βόρβορος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX: Je 45(38):6 (טִיט)* ;] mud, filth: 2Pe.2:22.† (AS)

borras.notes: βορρᾶς, -ᾶ (Attic contr. of Βορέας, the North wind personified), [in LXX for צָפוֹן ;] __1. Boreas, the North wind. __2. the north: Luk.13:29, Rev.21:13.† (AS)

bosko.notes: βόσκω, [in LXX for רעה ;] prop., of a herdsman, to feed: Mat.8:33, Mrk.5:14, Luk.8:34 15:15; metaphorically, of Christian pastoral care, Jhn.21:15, 17. Pass., of cattle, to feed, graze: Mat.8:30, Mrk.5:11, Luk.8:32.†…

bosor.notes: Βοσόρ see Βεώρ - ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בְּעוֹר), Beor, father of Balaam: 2Pe.2:15 (Rec. Βοσόρ).† (AS)

botane.notes: βοτάνη, -ῆς, ἡ (βόσκω), [in LXX for עֵשֶׂב, דֶשֶׁא, חָצִיר ;] __1. grass, fodder. __2. green herb: Heb.6:7.† SYN.: λάχανον, a garden herb, a vegetable. (AS)

bothunos.notes: βόθυνος, -ου, ὁ (= βόθρος, more frequently in cl.), [in LXX chiefly for פַּחַת ;] a pit: Mat.12:11 15:14, Luk.6:39 (cf. DB, iii, 885; DCG, ii, 367).† (AS)

botrus.notes: βότρυς, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX for אֶשְׁכֹּל ;] a cluster of grapes: Rev.14:18 (cf. στραφυλή) .† (AS)

boule.notes: βουλή, -ῆς, ἡ (βούλομαι), [in LXX frequently for עֵצָה ;] counsel, purpose (in cl., esp. of the gods): Luk.23:51, Act.4:28 5:38 19:1 27:12, 42; pl., 1Co.4:5; of the Divine purpose, Heb.6:17; τ. βουλὴν τ. θελήματος…

boulema.notes: βούλημα, -τος, τό (βούλομαι), [in LXX: Pro.9:10 (דַּעַת), 2Ma.15:5, 4Ma.8:18 * ;] purpose, will: Act.27:43, Rom.9:19, 1Pe.4:3.† SYN.: θέλημα. (AS)

bouleuo.notes: βουλεύω (βουλή), [in LXX chiefly for יעץ ;] to take counsel, deliberate, resolve. In mid., __1. to take counsel with oneself, consider: before εἰ, Luk.14:31. __2. to determine with oneself, resolve: with inf.,…

bouleutes.notes: βουλευτής, -οῦ, ὁ (βουλεύω), [in LXX: Job.3:14 12:17 (יעץ)* ;] a councillor, a senator; of a member of the Sanhedrin: Mrk.15:34, Luk.23:50.† (AS)

boulomai.notes: βούλομαι, [in LXX for חפץ, אבה, יעץ, etc. ;] to will, wish, desire, purpose, be minded, implying more strongly than θέλω (which see), the deliberate exercise of volition (see Hort on Jas.1:18): with inf. (M, Pr.,…

bounos.notes: βουνός, -οῦ, ὁ (a Cyrenaїc word, Hdt., iv, 199), [in LXX chiefly for גִּבְעָה ;] a hill: Luk.3:5 (LXX) 23:30.† (AS)

bous.notes: βοῦς, βοός, ὁ, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for בָּקָר ;] an ox, a cow: Luk.13:15 14:5, 19 Jhn.2:14, 15 1Co.9:9" (LXX), 1Ti.5:18.† (AS)

brabeion.notes: βραβεῖον, -ου, τό (βραβεύς, an umpire), a prize in the games: 1Co.9:24; metaphorically, of the Christian's reward, Php.3:14.† (AS)

brabeuo.notes: βραβεύω (βραβεύς, an umpire), [in LXX: Wis.10:12 * ;] __(a) prop., to act as umpire; hence, __(b) generally, to arbitrate, decide (Isocr., Dem.; Lft., Col., l.with; MM, see word): Col.3:15; __(with) in some late…

brachion.notes: βραχίων, -ὀνος, ὁ, [in LXX, β. Κυρίου, frequently for זְרוֹעַ יהוָֹה ;] the arm; as in OT, β. Κυρίου, metaphorically, for the Divine power: Luk.1:51, Jhn.12:38" (LXX), Act.13:17.† (AS)

brachus.notes: βραχύς, -εῖα, -ύ, [in LXX chiefly for מְעַט ;] short; __(a) of time; short, little: βραχύ, Act.5:34; μετὰ β., Luk.22:58; β. τι, a short time, Heb.2:7, 9 RV, mg.; __(b) of distance: Act.27:28; __(with) of quantity or…

braduno.notes: βραδύνω (βραδύς), [in LXX: Gen.43:10 (מההּ hith.), Deu.7:10, Isa.46:13 (אחר pi.), Si 32 (35):18 * ;] __1. trans., to retard (Soph., Is, l.with). __2. More frequently intrans., to be slow, to tarry: 1Ti.3:15,…

braduploeo.notes: βραδυπλοέω, -ῶ (βραδύς, πλοῦς), to sail slowly: Act.27:7.† (AS)

bradus.notes: βραδύς, -εῖα, -ύ, slow: εἰς τὸ λαλῆσαι, Jas.1:19; metaphorically, of the understanding: β. τ. καρδίᾳ, assoc. with ἀνόητος, Luk.24:25.† (AS)

bradutes.notes: 1. slowness , (Iliad by Homer), attic 2. of the mind, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

brecho.notes: βρέχω, [in LXX chiefly for מטר ;] __1. to wet: Luk.7:38, 44. __2. In late Gk. writers and vernac. = ὕειν, to send rain, to rain (Kennedy, Sources, 39, 155): Mat.5:45; trop., β. πῦρ κ. θεῖον, Luk.17:29; impers.,…

brephos.notes: βρέφος, -ους, τό, [in LXX: Sir.19:11, 1Ma.1:61, 2Ma.6:10, 3Ma.5:49, 4Ma.4:25 * ;] __1. an unborn child: Luk.1:41, 44. __2. a newborn child, a babe: Luk.2:12, 16 18:15, Act.7:19, 1Pe.2:2; ἀπὸ βρέφους, from infancy,…

broche.notes: βροχή, -ῆς, ἡ (βρέχω), [in LXX: Psa.67 (68):9, 104 (105):32 (גֶּשֶׁם)* ;] __1. = βροχετός, a wetting (in π., of irrigation in Egypt; Deiss., LAE, 77). __2. As in MGr. (Kennedy, Sources, 153), = ὑετός, rain: Mat.7:25,…

broma.notes: βρῶμα, -τος, τό (cf. βιβρώσκω), [in LXX chiefly for אֹכֶל ;] food: Rom.14:15, 20 1Co.8:8, 13 10:3; pl., Mat.14:15, Mrk.7:19, Luk.3:11 9:13, 1Co.6:13, 1Ti.4:3, Heb.9:10 13:9; trop., of spiritual food, Jhn.4:34,…

brosimos.notes: βρώσιμος, -ον (βρῶσις), [in LXX: Lev.19:23, Neh.9:25, Eze.47:12 (מַאֲכָל)* ;] eatable: Luk.24:41.† (AS)

brosis.notes: βρῶσις, -εως, ἡ (cf. βιβρώσκω), [in LXX chiefly for parts and derivatives of אכל ;] __1. eating: β. καὶ πόσις, Rom.14:17, Col.2:16 (see Lft., ICC, in l.); with genitive obj., 1Co.8:4; metaphorically, corrosion, rust:…

brucho.notes: βρύχω (Attic, βρύκω), [in LXX: Job.16:10(9), Psa.34 (35):16 36 (37):12 111 (112):10, La 2:16 (חרק)* ;] __1. to bite or eat greedily. __2. to gnash, grind, with the teeth: Act.7:54.† (AS)

brugmos.notes: βρυγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (βρύχω), [in LXX: Pro.19:12 (נַהַם), Sir.51:3 * ;] a biting, a gnashing of teeth: Mat.8:12 13:42, 50 22:13 24:51 25:30, Luk.13:28.† (AS)

bruo.notes: βρύω, poët., late prose and vernac., to be full to bursting; __1. of the earth producing vegetation. __2. Of plants putting forth buds. __3. Of springs, to gush with water: Jas.3:11.† (AS)

burseus.notes: βυρσεύς, -έως, ὁ (βύρσα, a hide), late form for βυρσοδέψης, a tanner: Act.9:43 10:6, 32.† (AS)

bussinos.notes: βύσσινος, -η, -ον (βύσσος), [in LXX chiefly for שֵׁשׁ, בּוּץ, etc. ;] made of βύσσος, fine linen: Rev.18:12, 16 19:8, 14.† (AS)

bussos.notes: βύσσος, -οῦ, ἡ (cf. Heb. בּוּץ), [in LXX chiefly for שֵׁשׁ, בּוּץ ;] byssus, a fine species of flax, also the linen made from it: Luk.16:19.† (AS)

buthizo.notes: βυθίζω (βυθός), [in LXX: 2Ma.12:4 * ;] trans., to cause to sink, to sink: metaphorically, εἰς ὄλεθρον, 1Ti.6:9; pass., to sink, intrans.: Luk.5:7.† (AS)

buthos.notes: βυθός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX: Exo.15:5, Neh.9:11 (מְצוֹלָה), Psa.67 (68):22 68 (69):2, 15 106 (107):24 (מְצוּלָה)* ;] __1. the bottom. __2. the depth of the sea, the deep sea: 2Co.11:25.† (AS)

chairo.notes: χαίρω [in LXX for שָׂמַח (Gen.45:16, al.), גִּיל (Pro.2:14, al.), etc.; inf., as greeting (see infr.), Isa.48:22 57:21 שָׁלוֹם), 1Ma.10:18, 2Ma.1:1 and frequently in these books ;] __1. to rejoice, be glad:…

chalao.notes: χαλάω, -ῶ [in LXX: (Jer.38:6) (שָׁלַח pi.), etc. ;] __(a) to slacken, loosen; __(b) to let loose, let go; __(with) to lower, let down: with accusative of thing(s), Mrk.2:4, Luk.5:4-5, Act.9:25 27:17, 30; with…

chalaza.notes: χάλαζα, -ης, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for בָּרָד ;] hail: Rev.8:7 11:19 16:21.† (AS)

chaldaios.notes: Χαλδαῖος, -ου, ὁ a Chaldæan: γῆ Χαλδαίων, Act.7:4.† (AS)

chalepos.notes: χαλεπός, -ή, -όν [in LXX: Isa.18:2 (יָרֵא), Wis.3:19, Sir.3:21, al. ;] hard; __(a) hard to do or deal with, difficult; __(b) hard to bear, painful, grievous: καιροί, 2Ti.3:1; __(with) of persons, hard to deal with,…

chalinagogeo.notes: χαλιναγωγέω, -ῶ (χαλινός, ἄγω), to lead with a bridle; metaphorically, to bridle, restrain: with accusative, γλῶσσαν, Jas.1:26; σῶμα, Jas.3:2.† (AS)

chalinos.notes: χαλινός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for מֶתֶג ;] a bridle: Jas.3:3, Rev.14:20.† (AS)

chalkedon.notes: χαλκηδών, -όνος, ὁ chalcedony, "supposed to denote a green silicate of copper found in the mines near Chalcedon " (Swete): Rev.21:19.† (AS)

chalkeos.notes: χάλκεος, -έα, -εον (-οῦς, -ῆ, -οῦν) (χαλκός), [in LXX chiefly for נְחֹשֶׁת ;] brazen (i.e. of copper): Rev.9:20.† (AS)

chalkeus.notes: χαλκεύς, -έως, ὁ (χαλκός), [in LXX for חָרָשׁ, etc. ;] a worker, in metal, esp. a copper-smith: 2Ti.4:14.† (AS)

chalkion.notes: χαλκίον, -ου, τό (χαλκός), [in LXX: Job.41:22(23) (סִיר), etc. ;] a brazen (copper) vessel: Mrk.7:4.† (AS)

chalkolibanos.notes: χαλκο-λίβανον, -ου, τό chalcolibanus, probably "a mixed metal of great brilliance" (Swete): Rev.1:15 2:18 (RV, burnished brass).† (AS)

chalkos.notes: χαλκός, -oῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for נְחֹשֶׁת ;] copper: 1Co.13:1, Rev.18:12; by meton., of copper coin, Mat.10:9, Mrk.6:8 12:41.† (AS)

chamai.notes: χαμαί adv., on or to the ground: Jhn.9:6 18:6.† (AS)

chanaan.notes: Χαναάν, ἡ indecl. (Heb. כְּנַעַן), Canaan: Act.7:11; γῆ Χ., Act.13:19.† (AS)

chara.notes: χαρά, -ᾶς, ἡ (χαίρω), [in LXX for שִׂמְחָה, שָׂשׂוֹן, etc. ;] joy, delight: Luk.1:14 15:7, 10, Jhn.15:11 16:22, 24 17:13, Act.8:8, 2Co.1:24 7:13 8:2, Gal.5:22, Col.1:11, Php.2:2, 1Jn.1:4, 2Jn.12; opposite to…

charagma.notes: χάραγμα, -τος, τό (χαράσσω, to engrave), __(a) a stamp, impress, mark: Rev.13:16-17 14:9, 11 16:2 19:20 20:4 (see Deiss., BS, 240 ff.); __(b) a thing graven: Act.17:29.† (AS)

charakter.notes: χαρακτήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ (χαράσσω, to engrave), [in LXX: Lev.13:28 (צָרֶבֶת), 2Ma.4:10, 4Ma.15:4 א R * ;] __1. a tool for graving. __2. a stamp or impress: as on a coin or seal; metaphorically, χ. τ. ὑποστάσεως, Heb.1:3.† (AS)

charax.notes: χάραξ, -ακος, ὁ (χαράσσω), [in LXX for סֹלְלָה, מָצוֹר, etc. ;] __1. a pointed stake __2. a palisade or rampart: Luk.19:43.† (AS)

charis.notes: χάρις, -ιτος, ἡ Abbott-Smith does not include the article here., accusative, χάριν (χάριτα in Act.24:27, Ju 4; see WH, App., 157), [in LXX chiefly for חֵן ;] __1. objectively, that which causes favourable regard,…

charisma.notes: χάρισμα, -τος, τό (χαρίζομαι) [in LXX: Sir.7:33 א (AB, χάρις) Sir.38:30 Bl (א AB2R, χρῖσμα) * ;] a gift of grace, a free gift, esp. of extra­ordinary operations of the Spirit in the Apostolic Church, but including…

charitoo.notes: χαριτόω, -ῶ (χάρις), [in LXX: Sir.18:17 (ἀνδρί κεχαριτωμένῳ; Vg., justificato; Syr., saintly) * ;] to endow with χάρις (which see), i.e. __1. (a) to make graceful; __(b) to make gracious (Sir, l.with). __2. In…

charizo.notes: χαρίζομαι (χάρις), [in LXX: Est.8:7 (נָתַן), Sng.1:4 א, Sir.12:3, 2 -4Ma.9:1-32 * ;] __1. to show favour or kindness: with dative of person(s), Gal.3:18. __2. to give freely, bestow: with accusative and dative,…

charran.notes: χαρράν indecl. (in FlJ., Ant., i, 16, 1, Κάρρα, -ας, ib. 6, 5, Χαρρά, -ᾶς; so LXX: Gen.29:4 E, Eze.27:28 B, elsewhere -άν­Heb. חָרָן), Haran, a town in N.W. Mesopotamia: Act.7:2, 4.† (AS)

chartes.notes: χάρτης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Isa.8:1 A, Jer.36:2, 6 36:23 (מְגִלָּה) * ;] a sheet of paper, made of papyrus strips (see Kennedy, Sources, 42; Milligan, NTD, 10-12; DB, iv, 945 f.): II Jn 12 (Plat., Inscr.).† (AS)

chasma.notes: χάσμα, -τος, τό (χάσκω, to yawn), [in LXX: 2Ki.18:17 (פַּחַת)* ;] a chasm, wide space: Luk.16:26.† (AS)

cheilos.notes: χεῖλος, -ους, τό, genitive pl., -εων (see Bl., § 8, 4; Thackeray, Gr., I, 151), [in LXX chiefly for שָׂפָה ;] a lip (as in Heb., of the lip as the organ of speech): Mat.15:8, Mrk.7:6, Rom.3:13, 1Co.14:21, Heb.13:15,…

cheimarros.notes: χείμμαρος (shortened form of the more usual -οος, Attic contr., -ους), -ον (χεῖμα, ῥέω) [in LXX chiefly for נַחַל ;] winter-flowing; as subst., ὁ χ. (sc. ποταμός), a torrent: Jhn.18:1.† (AS)

cheimazo.notes: χειμάζω (χεῖμα, winter cold) [in LXX: Pro.26:10 (†) * ;] __1. to expose to winter cold, go into winter quarters. __2. to drive with storm; pass., to be driven with storm, tempest-tossed: Act.27:18.† (AS)

cheimon.notes: χειμών, -ῶνος, ὁ [in LXX for גֶּשֶׁם, סְתָו ;] __1. winter: Jhn.10:22, 2Ti.4:21; genitive, χειμῶνος, in winter, Mat.24:20, Mrk.13:18. __2. Prop., a winter storm, hence, generally, a storm, tempest: Mat.16:3 (T, WH,…

cheir.notes: χείρ, genitive, χειρος (accusative, χεῖραν, 1Pe.5:6 T), ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for יָד ;] the hand: Mat.3:12, Mrk.3:1, Luk.6:6, al. mult.; ἡ χ., acting subject, Luk.22:21; pl., Act.17:25 20:34, 1Jn.1:1; τ. ἔργα τῶν χ.,…

cheiragogeo.notes: χειραγωγέω, -ῶ (χειραγωγός), [in LXX: Jdg.16:26 A (יָד חָזַק), Tob.11:16 א * ;] to lead by the hand: Act.9:8 22:11.† (AS)

cheiragogos.notes: χειρ-αγωγός, -όν (χείρ, ἄγω) leading by the hand. As subst., ὁ χ., one to lead by the head, a guide: Act.13:11.† (AS)

cheirographos.notes: χειρόγραφος, -ον (χείρ, γράφω), [in LXX: Tob.5:3 9:2, 5 * ;] written with the hand. As subst., τὸ χ., a handwriting (Inscr., Polyb., al.): metaphorically, Col.2:14.† (AS)

cheiron.notes: χείρων, -ον, compar. of κακός [in LXX: 1Ki.17:43 B, Wis.15:18 17:6, 3Ma.5:20 * ;] worse: Mat.9:16 12:45 27:64, Mrk.2:21, Luk.11:26, Jhn.5:14, 1Ti.5:8, Heb.10:29, 2Pe.2:20; εἰς (ἐπὶ) τὸ χεῖρον, Mrk.5:26, 2Ti.3:13.† (AS)

cheiropoietos.notes: χειρο-ποίητος, -ον (χείρ, ποιέω), [in LXX (of idols) for אֱלִיל ;] made by hand (i.e. of human handiwork): of temples, Mrk.14:58, Act.7:48 17:24, Heb.9:11, 24; of circumcision, Eph.2:11.† (AS)

cheirotoneo.notes: χειρο-τονέω, -ῶ (χείρ, τείνω) __1. to vote by stretching out the hand in the Athenian ἐκκλησία (Luc., Plut.). __2. to appoint: __(a) by vote, 2Co.8:19 __(b) without vote, Act.14:23 (see Rackham, in l) (cf.…

cheroubim.notes: Χερουβείν (Rec. -βίμ), τά (Heb. כְּרוּב), Cherubim: Heb.9:6 (cf. Exo.25:17 (18), al.; see DB, i, 377 ff.).† (AS)

chiliarchos.notes: χιλίαρχος (in Hdt., al., -ης), -ου, ὁ (χίλιοι, ἄρχω) [in LXX chiefly for אַלּוּף שַׂר ;] a chiliarch, the commander of a thousand, esp. a Roman military tribune, the commander of a cohort: Jhn.18:12, Act.21:31-33, 37…

chilias.notes: χιλιάς, -άδος, ἡ (χίλιοι), [in LXX for אֶלֶף ;] the number one thousand, a thousand: Luk.14:31, Act.4:4, 1Co.10:8, Rev.5:11 7:4-8 11:13 14:1, 3 21:16.† (AS)

chion.notes: χιών, -όνος, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁלֶג also (in Da) for תְּלַג ;] snow: Mat.28:3, Rev.1:14.† (AS)

chios.notes: χίος, -ου, ἡ Chios, an island in Ægean Sea: Act.20:15.† (AS)

chiton.notes: χιτών, ῶνος, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for כְּתֹנֶת:] the garment worn next the skin (though two tunics were sometimes worn, see Swete, Mk., 117), a tunic: Mat.10:10, Mrk.6:9 14:63, Luk.3:11 9:3, Ju 23; dieting. from ἱμάτιον…

chlamus.notes: χλαμύς, -ύδος, ἡ [in LXX: 2Ma.12:35 * ;] a chlamys, or short cloak worn over the χιτών (which see): Mat.27:28, 31 (see Tr., Syn., § 1).† (AS)

chleuazo.notes: χλευάζω (χλεύη, a jest), [in LXX: Wis.11:14, 2Ma.7:7, 4Ma.5:22 * ;] to jest, mock, jeer: Act.17:32.† (AS)

chliaros.notes: χλιαρός, -ά, -όν (χλίω, to become warm), warm, tepid; metaphorically, of persons, luke-warm: Rev.3:16.† (AS)

chloros.notes: χλωρός, -ά, -όν (χλόη), [in LXX for יֶרֶק, etc. ;] __(a) pale green: χόρτος, Mrk.6:39, Rev.8:7; πᾶν χ., Rev.9:4; __(b) pale: ἵππος, Rev.6:8.† (AS)

choikos.notes: χοϊκός, -ή, -όν, (χοῦς) earthy, made of dust: 1Co.15:47-49 (see Field, Notes, 179 f.).† (AS)

choinix.notes: χοῖνιξ, -ικος, ἡ [in LXX: Eze.45:10-11 (בַּת) * ;] a chænix, a dry measure of rather less than a quart: Rev.6:6 (EV, measure).† (AS)

cholao.notes: χολάω, -ῶ (χολή), [in LXX: 3Ma.3:1 R * ;] __1. to be melancholy mad (Aristoph.). __2. = χολοῦμαι, to be angry: with dative of person(s), Jhn.7:23.† (AS)

chole.notes: χολή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX for רֹאשׁ, לַעֲנָה, מְרֵרָה ;] gall: Mat.27:34 (here prob. = myrrh, cf. Mrk.15:23, see Swete, in l; DCG, i, 634); metaphorically, Act.8:23.† (AS)

choos.notes: χοῦς, -οός accusative, οῦν, ὁ, (contr. from χόος), [in LXX chiefly for עָפָר ;] __1. earth, soil. __2. In later writers (Pint., LXX), = κονιορτός, dust: Mrk.6:11, Rev.18:19.† (AS)

chora.notes: χώρα, -ας, ἡ [in LXX for אֶרֶץ, מְדִינָה, etc. ;] __1. most frequently in cl., a space, place. __2. land, i.e. __(a) a land, country, region: Mat.12:2, Mrk.5:10 6:55, Luk.2:8 15:13-15 19:12, Jhn.11:54, Act.13:49…

chorazin.notes: Χοραζείν (Rec. -ζίν), ἡ, Chorazin, a town of Galilee: Mat.11:21, Luk.10:13.† (AS)

choregeo.notes: χορηγέω, -ῶ (χορός, ἡγέομαι) [in LXX for כּוּל pilp. ;] __1. to lead a χορός (see LS, see word). __2. to defray the cost of a χορός. __3. In late writers, metaphorically, with accusative (see M, Pr., 65), to supply,…

choreo.notes: χωρέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Gen.13:6 (נָשָׂא), 3Ki.7:26 7:38 (כּוּל hi.), 2Ch.4:5 (חָזַק hi.), Wis.7:23-24, al. ;] __I. Intrans., __1. to make room, give way, retire, pass: before εἰς, Mat.15:17; metaphorically (EV, come),…

chorion.notes: χωρίον, -ου, τό (dimin. of χώρα, χῶρος), [in LXX: 1Ch.27:27 (כֶּרֶם), 2Ma.11:5 2Mac 12:7 2Mac 12:21, 4Ma.15:20 * ;] __1. a place, region. __2. an estate, property, piece of land: Mat.26:36, Mrk.14:32, Jhn.4:5,…

chorizo.notes: χωρίζω [in LXX: 2Ch.12:8, al. (בָּדַל ni., etc.), Wis.1:3, 2Ma.5:21, al. ;] __1. to separate, divide, put asunder: with accusative of thing(s), opposite to συζεύγνυμι Mat.19:6, Mrk.10:9; with accusative of person(s),…

choros.notes: χορός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for מָחוֹל, מְחֹלָה ;] a dance: pl., Luk.15:25.† (AS)

demiourgos.notes: δημιουργός, -οῦ, ὑ (δῆμος, ἔργον), [in LXX: 2Ma.4:1 * ;] __1. one who works for the people. __2. Univ., an author, builder, maker; the maker of the world (Xen., Mem., I, 4, 9, al.), Heb.11:10.† SYN.: κτίστης,…

demos.notes: δῆμος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁפָּחָה ;] __1. a district, country. __2. the common people, the people generally; esp. the people assembled: Act.12:22 17:5 19:30 33.† SYN.: λαός, the people at large: δ., the…

demosios.notes: δημόσιος, -α, -ον (δῆμος), [in LXX: 2Ma.6:10, 3Ma.2:27 4:7 * ;] belonging to the people, public: Act.5:18; dative fem. used adverbially (cl.); __(a) at the public expense, by public consent; __(b) publicly: Act.16:37…

denarion.notes: δηνάριον, -ου, τό the Lat. denarius, a Roman coin, nearly equal to the δραχμή, which see: Mat.18:28 20:2, 9, 13 22:19, Mrk.6:37 12:15 14:5, Luk.7:41 10:35 20:24, Jhn.6:7 12:5, Rev.6:6; τὸ ἀνὰ δ., Mat.20:10.† (AS)

dendron.notes: δένδρον, -ου, τό [in LXX for עֵץ, etc. ;] a tree: Mat.3:10, al.; δ. ἀγαθόν, Mat.7:17, 18; δ. καλόν, Mat.12:33, Luk.6:43; δ. σαπρόν, Mat.7:17, 18 12:33, Luk.6:43; γίνεσθαι δ., Mat.13:32; γ. εἰς δ., Luk.13:19. (AS)

deo.notes: δέω (I), [in LXX chiefly for אסר ;] to tie, bind, fasten; __(1) with accusative of thing(s), before εἰς δεσμάς, Mat.13:30; of an ass, Mat.21:2, Mrk.11:2, 4 Luk.19:30. __(2) with accusative of person(s), of swathing a…

deomai.notes: δέομαι (mid. of δέω, II, which see, as depon.) [in LXX for חנן, etc. ;] to want for oneself; __1. to want, need: __(a) absol.; __(b) with genitive __2. to beg, request, beseech, pray; __(i) in general: absol.,…

derbe.notes: Δέρβη, -ης, ἡ, Derbe, a city of Lycaonia: Act.14:6, 20 16:1.† (AS)

dermatinos.notes: δερμάτινος, -η, -ον (δέρμα), [in LXX for עוֹר ;] of skin, leathern: Mat.3:4, Mrk.1:6 (cf. 4Ki.1:8).† (AS)

dero.notes: δέρω [in LXX: Lev.1:6, 2Ch.29:34; 35:11 (פָּשַׁט hi.)* ;] __1. to skin, flay. __2. (of. Eng. slang, hide) to beat, thrash: with accusative, Mat.21:35, Mrk.12:3, 5, Luk.20:10, 11 22:63, Jhn.18:23, Act.5:40 16:37…

desme.notes: δέσμη (Rec. δεσμή), -ης, ἡ (δέω), [in LXX for אֲגֻדָּה, Exo.12:22 * ;] a bundle: δήσατε αὐτὰ εἰς δέσμας (D, Orig., omit εἰς, and Blass thinks original reading, δέσμας δέσμας; see Deiss., LAE, 125.4), Mat.13:30.† (AS)

desmeuo.notes: δεσμεύω (δεσμός), [in LXX for אָסַר (Jdg.16:11, al.), אָלַם pi. (Gen.37:7, al.), etc. ;] __1. to put in chains: Luk.8:29, Act.22:4. __2. to bind, tie together: φορτία, Mat.23:4.† (AS)

desmios.notes: δέσμιος, -ον (also -α, -ον; δεσμός), [in LXX for אסר;] __1. binding. __2. bound, captive; ὁ δ., as subst., a prisoner: Mat.27:15, 16, Mrk.15:6, Act.16:25, 27 23:18 25:14, 27 28:16 (Rec.) 17, Heb.10:34 13:3; ὁ δ. τοῦ…

desmophulax.notes: δεσμο-φύλαξ, -κος, ὁ (δεσμός, φύλαξ), a prison-keeper, gaoler: Act.16:23, 27, 36 (cf. ἀρχιδ-, Gen.39:21).† (AS)

desmos.notes: δεσμός, -οῦ, ὁ (δέω), [in LXX chiefly for אסר ;] a band, bond: metaphorically, Luk.13:16; ὁ δεσμὸς τ. γλώσσης, Mrk.7:35 (for this expression in π., see Deiss., LAE, 306 ff.; of actual bonds, see Ruth., Gr., 9). Pl.,…

desmoterion.notes: δεσμωτήριον, -ου, τό [in LXX for בֵּית סֹהַר (Ge), אָסִיר ;] a prison: Mat.11:2, Act.5:21, 23 16:26.† (AS)

desmotes.notes: δεσμώτης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for אסר, מַסְגֵּר ;] a prisoner: Act.27:1, 42.† (AS)

despotes.notes: δεσπότης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for אָדוֹן, אֲדֹנָי; in Jdth.9:17, δ. τ. οὐρανῶν κ. τ. γῆς]; a master, lord, correlative of δοῦλος, οἰκέτης: 1Ti.6:1, 2, 2Ti.2:21, Tit.2:9, 1Pe.2:18; as title of God, voc., δέσποτα…

deuteraios.notes: δευτεραῖος, -α, -ον (δεύτερος), adj. with adverbial sense; on the second day: δευτεραῖοι ἤλθομεν, Act.28:13.† (AS)

deuteros.notes: δεῦτερος, -α, -ον, second in order, with or without idea of time: Mat.22:26, 39, al.; θάνατος, Rev.2:11 20:14 21:8; χάρις, 2Co.1:15. In neut. as adv., secondly, a second time; opposite to πρῶτον: Jhn.3:4 21:16,…

dexiolabos.notes: δεξιολάβος, -ου, ὁ (δεξιός, λαμβάνω), a kind of soldier, prob. a spearman (Vg., lancearius) or slinger: Act.23:23.† δεξιο-βόλος, -ου, ὁ (δεξιός, βάλλω), one who throws with the right hand: L for δεξιολάβος,…

dexios.notes: δεξιός, -ά, -όν [in LXX chiefly for יָמִין ;] the right: Mat.5:29, Jhn.18:10, al.; ὅπλα δ., weapons carried in the right hand, i.e. for offence, 2Co.6:7 ; ἡ δ. χείρ, Mat.5:30, Luk.6:6, al.; ἡ δ. (sc. χείρ), Mat.6:3,…

diabaino.notes: δια-βαίνω [in LXX chiefly for עבר ;] __1. to make a stride. __2. to step across, cross over; __(a) trans.: τ. θάλασσαι, Heb.11:29; __(b) intrans.: before εἰς, Act.16:9; πρός, Luk.16:26.† (AS)

diaballo.notes: δια-βάλλω [in LXX: Dan LXX 3:8, Da TH 3:8; 6:24 (25) (אֲכַל קְרַץ), 2Ma.3:11, 4Ma.4:1 * ;] __1. to throw across. __2. To slander, defame, accuse falsely or maliciously: Luk.16:1 (Cremer, 120).† (AS)

diabebaioo.notes: δια-βεβαιόομαι, -οῦμαι to affirm confidently: Tit.3:8; before περί, 1Ti.1:7 (Cremer, 140).† (AS)

diablepo.notes: δια-βλέπω __1. to took straight before one. __2. to see clearly: Mat.7:5, Mrk.8:25, Luk.6:42 (cf. διάβλεψις, Aq., Isa.61:1, for LXX ἀνάβ-).† (AS)

diabolos.notes: διάβολος, -ον (διαβάλλω, which see) [in LXX for שָׂטָן (as Job.1:6), exc. Est.7:4 8:1 (צַר, צָרַר) ;] slanderous, accusing falsely. As subst., ὁ, ἡ, δ.; __(a) generally (of. Es, ll. with), a slanderer, false accuser:…

diacheirizo.notes: δια-χειρίζω (χείρ), to have in hand, conduct, manage. Mid. __(a) = act.; __(b) in late writers (Polyb., FlJ, al.), to lay hands on, kill: with accusative, Act.5:30 26:21.† (AS)

diachorizo.notes: δια-χωρίζω [in LXX: Gen.1:4 ff (בָּדַל hi.), Gen.13:9 ff. (פָּרַד ni.), etc. ;] to separate entirely. Mid., to separate oneself, depart: before ἀπό Luk.9:33.† (AS)

diadechomai.notes: δια-δέχομαι [in LXX for מִשְׁנֶה (Deiss., BS, 115), פַּרְבָּר ;] to receive through another, receive in turn: Act.7:45 (RV, in their turn; see Field, Notes, 116).† (AS)

diadema.notes: διάδημα, -τος, τό (διαδέω, to bind round), [in LXX for כֶּתֶר (as Est.1:11), etc. ;] the band round the τιάρα of a Persian king; a diadem, the badge of royalty: Rev.12:3 13:1 19:12.† SYN.: στέφανος, the badge of…

diadidomi.notes: δια-διδωμι [in LXX for חלק pi., etc. ;] __1. to hand over, deliver: Rev.17:13, Rec. __2. to distribute: Luk.11:22 18:22, Jhn.6:11, Act.4:35† (AS)

diadochos.notes: διά-δοχος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ (διαδέχομαι), [in LXX: 1Ch.18:17 (לְיַד), 2Ch.26:11 (שַׂר) 28:7 (מִשְׁנֶה), Sir.46:1 48:8, 2Ma.4:29 14:26 * ;] a successor: Act.24:27 (for usage in LXX and π. in sense of court official, see…

diaginomai.notes: δια-γίνομαι (Ion. and late Gk. for διαγίγν-), [in LXX, 2Ma.11:26 * ;] __1. to go through, to pass, e.g. τ. νύκτα; absol., to live. __2. Of time, to intervene, elapse: ptcp., with ἡμερῶν τινῶν, Act.25:13; ἱκανοῦ…

diaginosko.notes: δια-γινώσκω (see previous word), [in LXX chiefly for ידע, and cf. 2Ma.9:15 ;] __1. to distinguish, ascertain exactly: Act.23:15 __2. As Athen. law-term, to determine: τὰ καθ᾽ ὑμᾶς, your case, Act.24:22 (Cremer,…

diagnosis.notes: διά-γνωσις, -εως, ἡ (διαγιγνώσκω), [in LXX: Wis.3:18 * ;] __1. a distinguishing, also as medical term. __2. As law-term (Lat. cognitio), determination, decision: Act.25:21 (Cremer, 674).† (AS)

diago.notes: δι-άγω [in LXX for עבר hi., etc. ;] __1. to carry over. __2. Of time, to pass: βίον, 1Ti.2:2; absol., to live, before ἐν, Tit.3:3.† (AS)

diagonguzo.notes: δια-γογγύζω [in LXX chiefly for לין, לון, as Exo.16:2, and cf. Si 34(31):24 ;] of a number, to murmur or mutter among themselves: Luk.15:2 19:7.† (AS)

diagregoreo.notes: δια-γρηγορέω, -ῶ __(a) prop., to remain awake (R, mg.); __(b) to be fully awake (R, txt.): Luk.9:32.† (AS)

diaireo.notes: δι-αιρέω, -ῶ [in LXX for בּתר (as Gen.15:10), חלק (as Jos.18:5), etc. ;] __1. to divide into parts, cut asunder. __2. to distribute: with accusative of thing(s), dative of person(s), Luk.15:12, 1Co.12:11.† (AS)

diairesis.notes: δι-αίρεσις, -εως, ἡ (διαιρέω), [in LXX chiefly for מַחֲלֹקֶת ;] __1. a distinction, diference. __2. a division, distribution: 1Co.12:4-6 (cf. διαιρέω; Cremer, 616).† (AS)

diakatharizo.notes: δια-καθαρίζω = θαίρω: Mat.3:12.† δια-καθαίρω, to cleanse thoroughly: Luk.3:17.† (AS)

diakoluo.notes: δια-κωλεύω [in LXX: Jdth.4:7 12:7 * ;] to hinder, prevent: with accusative, Mat.3:14.† (AS)

diakoneo.notes: διακονέω, ῶ (δίακονος); __1. generally, to minister, serre, wait upon, especially at table, to do one a service, cure for one's needs: absol., Mat.20:28, Mrk.10:45, Luk.10:40 22:26, 27, Jhn.12:2, 1Pe.4:11; ὅσα…

diakonia.notes: διακονία, -ας, ἡ (διάκονος), [in LXX for נַעַר, שָׁרַת pi.: Est.6:3, Est.6:5 A; 1Ma.11:58 * ;] the office and work of a διάκονος, service, ministry; __(a) of domestic duties (Field, Notes, 63): Luk.10:40 __(b) spec.…

diakonos.notes: διάκονος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ (derivation unknown), [in LXX for נַעַר, שָׁרַת pi.: Est.6:3, 5, א B Est.1:10 2:2, Pro.10:4, 4Ma.9:17 * ;] __1. in general, a servant, attendant, minister: Mat.20:26 22:13 23:11, Mrk.9:35 10:43,…

diakosioi.notes: διακόσιοι, -αι, -α two hundred: Mrk.6:37, and al. (AS)

diakouo.notes: δι-ακούω [in LXX: Deu.1:16 (שׁמע), Job.9:33 (יָד שִׁית hi.)* ;] to hear through, hear fully; technically, to hear judicially (as De, l.with; of. Deiss., BS, 230): Act.23:35.† (AS)

diakrino.notes: δια-κρίνω [in LXX for שׁפט, דִּין, etc. ;] __1. to separate, hence, to distinguish, discriminate, discern: μηδὲν δ., Act.11:12; οὐδὲν δ. μεταξύ, Act.15:9; σε, 1Co.4:7; τὸ σῶμα, 1Co.11:29. __2. to settle, decide,…

diakrisis.notes: διά-κρισις, -εως, ἡ (διακρίνω) [in LXX for מִפְלָשׂ, Job.37:16 * ;] the act of judgment, discernment: Rom.14:1, 1Co.12:10, Heb.5:14.† (AS)

dialaleo.notes: δια-λαλέω, -ῶ [in Sm.: Ps 50(51):16, and al. ;] __1. to talk with: πρός, Luk.6:11. __2. to talk over: pass., Luk.1:65.† (AS)

dialego.notes: δια-λέγομαι (mid. of διαλέγω, to pick out, distinguish, as depon.), [in LXX: Exo.6:27, Isa.63:1 (דּבר pi.), Jdg.8:1 (ריב), 1Es.8:46, Est.5:2, Sir.14:20, 2Ma.11:20 * ;] to converse with, discourse (see Cl. Rev., i,…

dialeipo.notes: δια-λείπω [in LXX for יחל (as 1Ki.10:8), etc. ;] to intermit, leave off for a time: Luk.7:45.† (AS)

dialektos.notes: διά-λεκτος, -ου, ἡ (διαλέγομαι), [in LXX: Dan LXX 1:4 (לָשׁוֹן), Est.9:26 * ;] __1. conversation, discourse, speech (Plat., Dem., al.). __2. As in Polyb. and later writers, the language or dialect of a particular…

diallasso.notes: δι-αλλάσσω [in LXX: 1Ki.29:4 (רָצָה hithp.), I Est.4:31, al. ;] __1. to change, exchange. __2. to change enmity for friendship, to reconcile: pass., with dative of person(s), Mat.5:24. "The word denotes mutual…

dialogismos.notes: δια-λογισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (διαλογίζομαι) [in LXX chiefly for מַחֲשָׁבָה ;] a thought, reasoning, inward questioning: Mat.15:19, Mrk.7:21, Luk.2:35 5:22 6:8 9:46, 47 24:38, Rom.1:21 14:1, 1Co.3:20" (LXX), Php.2:14; κριταὶ…

dialogizomai.notes: δια-λογίζομαι, depon. [in LXX chiefly for חשׁב, frequently in Pss. ;] __1. to balance accounts (Dem.). __2. to consider, reason (Isocr.): Luk.1:29 5:21; ἐν τ. καρδία, Mrk.2:6, 8, Luk.5:22; περί Luk.3:15; ἐν ἑαυτῷ…

dialuo.notes: δια-λύω [in LXX for אבה, חבל, etc. ;] to part asunder, dissolve; of an assembly, pass., to disperse: Act.5:36.† (AS)

diamachomai.notes: δια-μάχομαι [in LXX for לחם ni., Dan LXX 10:20; Sir.8:1, 3 38:28 51:19 * ;] __1. to struggle against. __2. In argument, to contend: Act.23:9.† (AS)

diamarturomai.notes: δια-μαρτύρομαι, depon., of Ionic origin, intensive of the simple μαρτύρομαι, which see, [in LXX chiefly for עוּד hi., usually with dative of person(s), Deu.4:26 8:19, 1Ki.8:9, al. ;] solemnly to protest: Luk.16:28,…

diameno.notes: δια-μένω [in LXX for עמד, etc.;] to remain, continue: Luk.1:22 22:28, Gal.2:5, Heb.1:11" (LXX), 2Pe.3:4.† (AS)

diamerismos.notes: δια-μερισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (διαμερίζω), [in LXX: Eze.48:29 (מַחֲלֹקֶת), Mic.7:12 * ;] a division: opposite to εἰρήνη, Luk.12:51.† (AS)

diamerizo.notes: δια-μερίζω [in LXX chiefly for חלק pi. ;] __1. to distribute: with dative of person(s), Act.2:45; before εἰς, Luk.22:17, pass., Act.2:3. Mid. to distribute among themselves: Mat.27:35, Mrk.15:24, Luk.23:34; with…

dianemo.notes: δια-νέμω [in LXX for חלק, Deu.29:25 * ;] to distribute, divide: pass., to be spread about, Act.4:17.† (AS)

dianeuo.notes: δια-νεύω [in LXX: Ps 34(35):19 (קרץ), Sir.27:22 * ;] to wink at, nod to, beckon to: Luk.1:22.† (AS)

diangello.notes: δι-αγγέλω [in LXX for ספר pi., etc. ;] to publish abroad, proclaim: with accusative, Luk.9:60, Act.21:26, Rom.9:17" (LXX) .† (AS)

dianoema.notes: δια-νόημα, -τος, τό (διανοέομαι, to think), [in LXX for מַחֲשָׁבָה, etc., Isa.55:9, al., frequently in Sir ;] a thought: Luk.11:17.† (AS)

dianoia.notes: διάνοια, -ας, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for לֵב, לֵבָב ;] the understanding, mind: Luk.1:51, Eph.4:18, Col.1:21, 1Pe.1:13, 2Pe.3:1, 1Jn.5:20; pl., Eph.2:3; in quotations from LXX, Mat.22:37, Mrk.12:30, Luk.10:27, Heb.8:10…

dianoigo.notes: δι-αν-οίγω [in LXX for פֶּטֶר (Ex, Nu), פָּקַח, פָּתַח, etc. ;] to open up completely, to open: Luk.2:23 (LXX); pass., Mrk.7:34, Act.7:56. Metaphorical, δ. τ. νοῦν, Luk.24:45, τ. καρδίαν, Act.16:14, pass., οἱ…

dianuktereuo.notes: δια-νυκτερεύω (cf. διημερεύω, to pass the day) [in LXX: Job.2:9 * ;] to pass the night: before ἐν τ. προσευχῆ, Luk.6:12.† (AS)

dianuo.notes: δι-ανύω [in LXX: 2Ma.12:17 * ;] __1. to accomplish fully, finish, complete: Act.21:7 (EV). __2. In late writers (Xen., al., Clem., I ad Cor., xxv, 3), to continue: Ac, l.with (Field, Notes, 134f.).† (AS)

diaperao.notes: δια-περάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Deu.30:13, Isa.23:2 (עבר), עבר), 1Ma.6:1-63 * ;] to pass over, cross over: Mat.9:1; before ἐπὶ τ. γῆν, Mat.14:34, Mrk.6:53; εἰς, Mrk.5:21, Act.21:2; πρὸς ἡμᾶς, Luk.16:28.† (AS)

diaphemizo.notes: δια-φημίζω in late writers only, to spread abroad: τ. λόγον (= דָּבָר, the matter), Mrk.1:45, Mat.28:15; with accusative of person(s), to spread abroad one's fame: Mat.9:31.† (AS)

diaphero.notes: δια-φέρω [in LXX for שְׁנָא (שְׁנָא (Dan.7:1-28 only); 1Ki.17:39, Est.3:13, al. ;] __1. trans., __(a) to carry through: before διά, Mrk.11:16; __(b) to carry about, spread abroad: pass., Act.13:49 27:27. __2.…

diapheugo.notes: δια-φεύγω [in LXX: Jos.8:22 (פָּלִיט), Jos.10:28 (שָׂרִיד), etc. ;] to flee through, escape: Act.27:42.† (AS)

diaphoros.notes: διά-φορος, -ον (διαφέρω), [in LXX for שְׁנָא (Dan.7:7, 19); also as in Polyb., iv, 188, al., Τὸ δ., τὰ δ., money: Sir.27:1 42:5, 2Ma.3:6 ;] __1. different: Rom.12:6, Heb.9:10. __2. excellent: compar., -ώτερος,…

diaphtheiro.notes: δια-φθείρω [in LXX chiefly for שָׁחַת hi. ;] __1. to destroy utterly: Luk.12:33, Rev.11:18; pass., to be destroyed, disabled: Rev.8:9, 2Co.4:16. __2. In moral sense, to corrupt, deprave: τ. γῆν, Rev.11:18; pass.,…

diaphthora.notes: δια-φθορὰ, -ᾶς, ἡ (διαφθείρω), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁחַת, and cogn. forms ;] __1. destruction. __2. corruption (physical or moral): of the grave, Act.2:27 (LXX), Act.2:31 13:34-37.† (AS)

diaphulasso.notes: δια-φυλάσσω [in LXX chiefly for שָׁמַר (as Psa.91:11) ;] to guard carefully (M, Pr., 116), defend: with accusative, Luk.4:10 (LXX).† (AS)

diapleo.notes: to sail across , Thuc.; εἰς Αἴγιναν (Aristophanes Comicus): metaphorically, δ. βίον to make life's voyage , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

diaponeo.notes: δια-πονέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Ecc.10:9 (עָצַב ni.), 2Ma.2:28; in Aq.: Gen.6:6, 1Ki.20:3 * ;] to work out with labour. Pass., to be worn out, sore troubled: Mrk.14:4 (WH, mg.), Act.4:2 16:18.† (AS)

diaporeo.notes: δι-απορέω, -ῶ [in Sm.: Psa.77:5, Dan.2:1 * ;] to be quite at a loss, be in great perplexity: absol., Act.2:12; before διὰ τό, with inf., Luk.9:7; περί, Act.5:24; ἐν ἑαυτῷ, Act.10:17.† (AS)

diaporeuo.notes: δια-πορεύω [in LXX for עָבַר, הָלַךְ, etc. ;] to carry over. Pass., to pass across, journey through: absol., Luk.18:36, Rom.15:24; before κατὰ πόλεις κ. κώμας, Luk.13:22; διά, with genitive, Mrk.2:23, Luk.6:1 (cf.…

diapragmateuomai.notes: δια-πραγματεύομαι , "perfective compound" (see M, Pr., 118); __1. to examine thoroughly (Plat.). __2. In late writers (Dion. Hal.), to gain by trading: Luk.19:15.† (AS)

diaprio.notes: δια-πρίω [in LXX: 1Ch.20:3 (סוּר) * ;] to saw asunder. Pass., metaphorically (vernacular?), EV, cut to the heart: Act.5:33; before τ. καρδίαις αὐτῶν, Act.7:54.† (AS)

diarpazo.notes: δι-αρπάζω [in LXX for בָּזַז, גָּזַל, שָׁסַס, etc. ;] to plunder: Mat.12:29, Mrk.3:27.† (AS)

diarregnumi.notes: δια-ρήσσω (so WH, exc. Ac, l.with), δια-ρρήσσω (poetic and late form of διαρρήγνυμι), [in LXX chiefly for קָרָא ;] to break asunder, burst, rend: δεσμά, Luk.8:29; pass., δίκτυα, Luk.5:6; ἱμάτια, χιτῶνας, in grief or…

eidolothutos.notes: εἰδωλόθυτος, -ον, (εἴδωλον, θύω), [in LXX: 4Ma.5:2 * ;] sacrificed to idols: τὸ, τὰ εἰ, Act.15:29 21:25, 1Co.8:1, 4 7, 10 10:19, Rev.2:14, 2o.† (AS)

eidos.notes: εἶδος, -ους, τό, [in LXX for מַרְאֶה,, etc. ;] __1. that which is seen, appearance, external form: Luk.3:22 9:29, Jhn.5:37, 2Co.5:7 (ICC in l.). __2. form, sort, kind: 1Th.5:22.† (AS)

eike.notes: εἰκῇ (-ῆ, Rec., as in cl.), adv., [in LXX: Pro.28:25 (εἰκῇ)* ;] __1. without cause or reason: Mat.5:22 (E, mg.), Col.2:18 (ICC). __2. vainly, fruitlessly, to no purpose: Rom.13:4, 1Co.15:2, Gal.3:4 4:11, Col.2:18.† (AS)

eiko.notes: εἴκω, [in LXX: 2Ki.12:7 (ענה), Wis.18:25, 4Ma.1:6 * ;] to yield: Gal.2:5 (cf. ὑπ-είκω).† (AS)

eikon.notes: εἰκών, -όνος (cf. ἔοικα), [in LXX chiefly for צֶלֶם ;] an image, likeness: Mat.22:20, Mrk.12:16, Luk.20:24, Rom.1:23, 1Co.15:49, Rev.13:14, 15 14:9, 11 15:2 16:2 19:20 20:4; opposite to σκιά, Heb.10:1; of man, εἰ.…

eikosi.notes: εἴκοσι (never -ιν in WH, cf. Bl., §5, 3, and note), indecl., οἱ, αἱ, τά, twenty: Luk.14:31, Jhn.6:19, Act.1:15 27:28, 1Co.10:8, Rev.4:4, 10 5:8 11:16 19:4.† (AS)

eilikrineia.notes: εἰλικρινία (Rec., cl., -κρινεία), -ας, ἡ (εἰλικρινής), [in LXX: Wis.7:25 A * ;] sincerity, purity: 1Co.5:8, 2Co.1:12 2:17.† (AS)

eilikrines.notes: εἰλικρινής, -ές, [in LXX: Wi 72^ kB * ;] unalloyed, pure (Lat. sincerus; see DCG, ii, 635a); __(a) of unmixed substances; __(b) of abstract ideas; __(with) of ethical purity: Php.1:10, 2Pe.3:1.† SYN.: ἁγνός (which…

eiper.notes: εἴ-περ, see: εἰ. εἰ, conjunctive particle, used in conditions and in indirect questions. __I. Conditional, if; __1. with indic, expressing a general assumption; __(a) pres.: before indic, pres., Mat.11:14, Rom.8:25,…

eirene.notes: εἰρήνη, -ης, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלוֹם ;] peace; __1. of public peace, freedom from war: Luk.14:32, Act.12:20 24:2; of the church, Ac 9:31. __2. Of peace between persons, concord, agreement : Mat.10:34,…

eireneuo.notes: εἰρηνεύω (εἰρήνη), [in LXX chiefly for שׁלם, שׁקט ;] __1. to bring to peace, reconcile (so 1Ma.6:60). __2. to keep peace, be at peace: Mrk.9:50, Rom.12:18, 2Co.13:11, 1Th.5:13 (cf. Sir.28:9; Cremer, 246).† (AS)

eirenikos.notes: είρηνικός, -ή, -όν (εἰρήνη), [in LXX for שָׁלוֹם and cognates ;] peaceful: Heb.12:11, Jas.3:17.† (AS)

eirenopoieo.notes: εἰρηνο-ποιέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Pro.10:10 * ;] to make peace: Col.1:20.† (AS)

eisago.notes: εἰσ-άγω [in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא, hi. ;] to bring in: with accusative, Luk.2:27, Jhn.18:16, Act.7:45; before εἰς, Luk.22:54, Act.9:8 21:28-29, 37 22:24, Heb.1:6; ὧδε, Luk.14:21.† (AS)

eisakouo.notes: είσ-ακούω [in LXX chiefly for שָׁמַע, also for עָנָה, etc. ;] to listen to, in two senses; __(a) to obey: 1Co.14:21 (cf. Deu.1:43, Sir.3:6) __(b) to listen, assent to; pass., to be heard: of persons praying, Mat.6:7,…

eisdechomai.notes: εἰσ-δέχομαι [in LXX for קָבַץ ;] to admit, receive: 2Co.6:17 (LXX) (Cremer, 687).† (AS)

eiseimi.notes: εἴσ-ειμι [in LXX for בּוֹא ;] to go in, enter: before εἰς, Act.3:3 21:26, Heb.9:6; πρὸς Ἰάκωβον, Act.21:18.† (AS)

eiskaleo.notes: εἰσ-καλέω, -ῶ, to call in: mid., with accusative of person(s), Act.10:23.† (AS)

eisodos.notes: εἴσ-οδος, -ου, ὁ (ὁδός) [in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא ;] __1. a means of entering, place of entrance: Heb.10:19, 2Pe.1:11 (cf. Westc., He., l.with; MM, Exp., xii; but see infr.). __2. a going in, entrance: Act.13:24;…

eispedao.notes: εἰσ-πηδάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Amo.5:19 (בּוֹא), Da TH Sus 1:26* ;] to spring in, rush in: Act.14:14 (Rec.), Act.16:29 (for exx. from π., see MM, Exp., xii).† (AS)

eisphero.notes: εἰσ-φέρω [in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא hi. ;] to bring in, into: with accusative of person(s), Luk.5:18-19; before εἰς, Mat.6:13, Luk.11:4; ἐπί, Luk.12:11; with accusative of thing(s), before εἰς, 1Ti.6:7; pass.,…

eisporeuo.notes: εἰσ-πορεύομαι [in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא ;] to go into, enter: Luk.8:16 11:33 19:30; before εἰς, Mrk.1:21 6:56 11:2, Luk.22:10, Act.3:2; πρός, with accusative of person(s), Act.28:30; ὅπου, Mrk.5:40; κατά τ. οἴκους,…

eistrecho.notes: εἰσ-τρέχω [in LXX: 2Ma.5:26 * ;] to run in: Act.12:14.† (AS)

eita.notes: εἶτα adv., denoting sequence; __1. of time; then, next: Mrk.8:25, Luk.8:12, Jhn.13:5 19:27 20:27, 1Ti.3:10, Jas.1:15; before genitive abs., Mrk.4:17; in enumerations, 1Co.15:5 15:7 15:24, 1Ti.2:13. __2. In argument;…

eite.notes: εἴτε, see: εἰ. εἰ, conjunctive particle, used in conditions and in indirect questions. __I. Conditional, if; __1. with indic, expressing a general assumption; __(a) pres.: before indic, pres., Mat.11:14, Rom.8:25,…

ekballo.notes: ἐκ-βάλλω [in LXX chiefly for גָּרַשׁ pi., also for שָׁלַךְ hi., יָצָא hi., יָרַשׁ hi., etc. ;] __1. to drive, cast or send out, to expel: with accusative of thing(s), mid. (σῖτον), before εἰς, Act.27:38; pass.,…

ekbasis.notes: ἔκ-βασις, -εως, ἡ (ἐκβαίνω), [in LXX: Wis.2:17 8:8 11:14 * ;] __1. a way out (Hom., Xen.): 1Co.10:13. __2. the issue (Menand.) Heb.13:7.† (AS)

ekbole.notes: ἐκ-βολή, -ῆς (ἐκβάλλω), [in LXX: Exo.11:1 (גָּרַשׁ), Jos.1:5 (ἐκβολὴν ποιεῖσθαι, טול hi.), Eze.47:8 (יָצָא)* ;] __1. a throwing out. __2. a jettison, a throwing overboard of cargo: Act.27:18 (cf. Jos, l.with; and see…

ekdechomai.notes: ἐκ-δέχομαι [in LXX for עֶרֶב, קָבַץ, etc. ;] __1. to take or receive from (Hom., Hdt., a1.). __2. (Rare in cl.), to expect, await: with accusative of thing(s), Jhn.5:3, Heb.11:10, Jas.5:7; with accusative of…

ekdemeo.notes: ἐκ-δημέω, -ῶ (ἔκδημος, from home; cf. -ία, 3Ma.4:11)*; to be from home, absent: 2Co.5:6; before ἀπό, 2Co.5:8; before ἐκ, 2Co.5:9 (cf. ἀπο-, ἐνδημέω).† (AS)

ekdidomi.notes: ἐκ-δίδωμι [in LXX for נָתַן, etc. ;] __1. to surrender, give up, give out. __2. to let out for hire (Hdt.); mid. (as frequently in π.; see MM, Exp., xii); to let out to one's advantage, Mat.21:33, 41, Mrk.12:1,…

ekdiegeomai.notes: ἐκ-δι-ηγέομαι, -οῦμαι depon., [in LXX chiefly for סָפַר, pi. ;] to tell in detail, relate, declare: Act.13:41 (LXX) Act.15:3.† (AS)

ekdikeo.notes: ἐκδικέω, -ῶ (ἔκδικος), [in LXX for פָּקַד, נָקַם, שָׁפַט, etc. ;] __1. to vindicate: with accusative of person(s), Luk.18:3, 5. __2. to avenge: with accusative of person(s), ἑαυτούς, Rom.12:19; with accusative of…

ekdikos.notes: ἔκδικος, -ον (δίκη), [in LXX: Wis.12:12, Sir.30:6, 4Ma.15:29 * ;] __1. without law, unjust. __2. exacting penalty from; as subst., an avenger: Rom.13:4; before περί, 1Th.4:6 (in π., a legal representative; Milligan,…

ekdotos.notes: ἔκ-δοτος, -ον (ἐκδίδωμι), [in LXX: Da TH Bel 1:22 * ;] given up, delivered over: Act.2:23 (for construction, see Field, Notes, 111 f.).† (AS)

ekkakeo.notes: ἐκκακέω, -ῶ, see: ἐνκακέω.ἐν-κακέω, -ῶ (LTr., ἐγκ-; Rec. ἐκκ-; cf. WH, Notes, 157 f.; κακός, cowardly), [in Sm.: Gen.27:46, Num.21:5, Pro.3:11, Isa.7:16 *;] to lose heart : Luk.18:1, 2Co.4:1,16, Gal.6:9, Eph.3:13,…

ekkathairo.notes: ἐκ-καθαίρω [in LXX for בָּעַר, etc. ;] __1. to cleanse thoroughly, cleanse out: with accusative, ἑαυτόν, 2Ti.2:21; of the impurity removed, ζυμήν, 1Co.5:7.† (AS)

ekkenteo.notes: ἐκ-κεντέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for דָּקַר ;] __1. to prick out, put out (Arist.). __2. to pierce (Polyb., LXX): with accusative of person(s), Jhn.19:37 (LXX), Rev.1:7.† (AS)

ekkleio.notes: ἐκ-κλείω [in LXX: ἐ. κρίσιν, for נָטָה hi., Exo.23:2 (also as seel., Job.34:20, Psa.67:1-7 (Psa.68:30) * ;] to shut out: Gal.4:17. Pass., Rom.3:27.† (AS)

ekklino.notes: ἐκ-κλίνω [in LXX for נָטָה, סוּר, etc. ;] intrans., to turn aside, turn away: metaphorically, from the right path, absol., Rom.3:12 (LXX); from evil, absol., 1Pe.3:11; before ἀπό, with genitive of person(s),…

ekkolumbao.notes: to swim out of , with genitive, (Euripides) (ML)

ekkomizo.notes: ἐκ-κομίζω to carry out: as freq., a corpse for burial, Luk.7:12.† (AS)

ekkopto.notes: ἐκ-κόπτω, [in LXX for כָּרַת, etc. ;] to cut out, cut off, cut down: of a hand, foot, Mat.5:30 18:8; a tree, Mat.3:10 7:19 Luk.3:9 13:7, 9; figuratively, of a branch, Rom.11:22; before ἐκ, Rom.11:24; metaphorically,…

ekkremannumi.notes: ἐκ-κρέμαννυμι, [in LXX for קָשַׁר, Gen.44:30 * ;] to hang from or upon; mid., ἐκκρέμαμαι: figuratively, ἐξεκρέματο αὐτοῦ άκούων (Rec.; WH read ἐξεκρέμετο, which implies a Pres. ἐκκρέμομαι, otherwise unknown; cf.…

eklaleo.notes: ἐκ-λαλέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Jdth.11:9 * ;] to speak out, divulge: Act.23:22.† (AS)

eklampo.notes: ἐκ-λάμπω [in LXX for אוֹר hi., etc. ;] to shine forth: Mat.13:43.† (AS)

eklanthano.notes: ἐκ-λανθάνω [in Sm.: Psa.13:2 * ;] to escape notice utterly; mid., to forget utterly: Heb.12:5.† (AS)

eklego.notes: ἐκ-λέγω [in LXX chiefly for בָּחַר ;] to pick out, choose. In NT always mid. (exc. Luk.9:35, ἐκλελεγμένος, WH, ἀγαπητός, R, mg.), to pick out for oneself, choose (cf. M, Pr., 157 f.): with accusative of thing(s),…

eklektos.notes: ἐκ-λεκτός, -ή, -όν (ἐκλέγω), [in LXX for בָּחַר (so prob. in Isa.28:16, Pro.17:3, for MT בָּחַן), בָּרִיא, etc. ;] __1. choice, select (cl., rarely; Thuc., Plat., al.), hence, eminent: Rom.16:13 (cf. Eze.27:24). __2.…

ekluo.notes: ἐκ-λύω [in LXX for רָפָה, etc. ;] __1. to loose, release. __2. to unloose, as a bow-string, to relax, enfeeble; pass., to be faint, grow weary: Mat.15:32, Mrk.8:3; of mental weariness, Gal.6:9, Heb.12:3, 5" (LXX) .† (AS)

ekmasso.notes: ἐκ-μάσσω [in LXX: Sir.12:11, Ep. Jer.13:1-27 24:1-10 * ;] to wipe off: with accusative, Luk.7:38, 44, Jhn.11:2 12:3 13:5.† (AS)

ekmukterizo.notes: ἐκ-μυκτηρίζω [in LXX: Psa.2:4 22:7 35:16 (לָעַג), I Est.1:51 A* ;] to hold up the nose in derision at, scoff at: with accusative, Luk.16:14 23:35.† (AS)

eknepho.notes: ἐκ-νήφω [in LXX: Gen.9:24, Hab.2:7 (יָקַץ), Jol.1:5, Hab.2:19 (יָקַץ hi.), 1Ki.25:37 (יָצָא), Sir.31:2 * ;] to become sober after drunkenness: metaphorically, of sobriety of mind, 1Co.15:34.† (AS)

ekneuo.notes: ἐκ-νεύω [in LXX: Jdg.4:18 (סוּר) Jdg.18:26, 4Ki.2:24 23:16 (פָּנָה), Mic.6:14 (סוּג hi.), 3Ma.3:22 * ;] __1. to bend the head aside (Xen.). __2. __(a) to shun, avoid (Diod.); __(b) to withdraw: Jhn.5:13† (AS)

ekpeirazo.notes: ἐκ-πειράζω [in LXX: Deu.6:16 8:2, 16 Psa.78:18 (נָסָה pi.) * ;] = cl. ἐκπειράομαι, to put to the proof or test, make trial of, tempt: with accusative, of God, Mat.4:7 (LXX), Luk.4:12 (ib.), 1Co.10:9; of Christ,…

ekpempo.notes: ἐκ-πέμπω [in LXX for שָׁלַח ;] to send forth: Act.13:4 17:10.† (AS)

ekpetazo.notes: ἐκ-πετάννυμι [in LXX chiefly for פָּרַשׂ, as Isa.65:2 (hithp.) ;] to spread out (as a sail), stretch forth: Rom.10:21(LXX).† (AS)

ekphero.notes: ἐκ-φέρω [in LXX chiefly for יָצָא hi. ;] __1. to carry out, bring out: with accusative of thing(s), Luk.15:22, 1Ti.6:7; with accusative of person(s), Mrk.8:23, Act.5:15; of the dead for burial (cf. κομίζω), Act.5:6,…

ekpheugo.notes: ἐκ-φεύγω [in LXX for נוּס, etc. ;] to flee away, escape: absol., Act.16:27, 1Th.5:3, Heb.2:3; before ἐκ, Act.19:10; with accusative of person(s), Heb.12:25; with accusative of thing(s), Luk.21:36, Rom.2:3; τ. χεῖρας…

ekphobeo.notes: ἐκ-φοβέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for חָרֵד hi. ;] to frighten away, terrify: with accusative of person(s), 2Co.10:9.† (AS)

ekphobos.notes: ἔκφοβος, -ον [in LXX: ἔ. εἶναι for יָגֹר, Deu.9:19; also 1Ma.13:2 * ;] affrighted, terrified: Mrk.9:16, Heb.12:21.† (AS)

ekphuo.notes: ἐκ-φύω [in OT (Sm.) Psa.104:14; (Al.) Isa.61:11 * ;] to cause to grow out, put forth (leaves): Mat.24:32, Mrk.13:28.† (AS)

ekpipto.notes: ἐκ-πίπτω [in LXX: Isa.40:8 28:1, 4 (הֶבֶל), Job.14:2 (מָלַל, see RV. mg), Job.15:30 (סוּר), Job.15:33 (שָׁלַךְ hi.), etc. ;] to fall out of, fall from, fall off: before ἐκ τ. χειρῶν, Act.12:7; absol., Act.27:32; of…

ekpleroo.notes: ἐκ-πληρόω [in LXX: 2Ma.8:10, 3Ma.1:2 3Mac 1:22 * ;] __1. to fill full, make up a number. __2. to fulfil (MM, Exp., xii; Cremer, 839), Act.13:32.† (AS)

epaischunomai.notes: ἐπ-αισχύνομαι [in LXX: Job.34:19 (נָשָׂא), Psa.119:6 (בּוּשׁ), Isa.1:29 A (חָפֵר) * ;] to be ashamed (of): absol., 2Ti.1:12; with accusative of person(s), Mrk.8:38, Luk.9:26; with accusative of thing(s), Rom.1:16,…

epaiteo.notes: ἐπ-αιτέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Psa_109:10 (H7592) Sir_40:28 * ;] __1. to ask besides. __2. to beg (as a mendicant; cf. MM, Exp., xiv): Luk.16:3 18:35 (Cremer, 74).† (AS)

epakoloutheo.notes: ἐπ-ακολουθέω, -ῶ [in LXX (chiefly metaphorically) for אָחַר, הָלַךְ, etc. ;] to follow after; in NT metaphorically; absol.: Mrk.16:20 (illustrated by use in verifying accounts; see MM, Exp., xiv; Milligan; NTD, 78);…

epakouo.notes: ἐπ-ακούω [in LXX for שָׁמַע, עָנָה, etc. ;] __1. to listen to. __2. to hearken to, hear with favour (one's prayer): with genitive of person(s), 2Co.6:2 (LXX).† (AS)

epakroaomai.notes: ἐπ-ακροάομαι, -ῶμαι to listen attentively: Act.16:25 (cf. Page, in l).† (AS)

epanagkes.notes: ἐπανάγκης, -ες (ἀνάγκη), only in neut.; __1. ἐπάναγκες (sc. ἐστί), it is compulsory, necessary. __2. As adv., of necessity: Act.15:28.† (AS)

epanago.notes: ἐπ-αν-άγω [in LXX: Zec.4:12 (רוּק hi.), Sir.17:26 26:28, 2Ma.9:21 2Mac 12:4 * ;] to bring up or back (sc. ναῦς); to put out to sea (DB, iii, 63b): Luk.5:3-4; intrans., to return: Mat.21:18.† (AS)

epanamimnesko.notes: ἐπ-ανα-μιμνήσκω to remind again: with accusative of person(s), Rom.15:15.† (AS)

epanapauo.notes: ἐπ-ανα-παύω [in LXX, mid., for נוּחַ, שָׁעַן ni ;] to refresh, cause to rest (upon); mid., to rest upon: metaphorically, with dative, Rom.2:17; before ἐπί, with accusative, Luk.10:6 (Cremer, 827).† (AS)

epanerchomai.notes: ἐπ-αν-έρχομαι [in LXX for שׁוּב, etc. ;] to return: Luk.10:35 19:15.† (AS)

epangelia.notes: ἐπ-αγγελία, -ας, ἡ (ἐπαγγέλλω), [in LXX: Psa.56:8 (סֵפֶר), etc. ;] __1. a summons (as Attic law-term, Dem., al.). __2. a promise (Dem., Arist., al.): Act.23:21; esp. in NT of the divine promises, Act.7:17, Rom.4:14,…

epangello.notes: ἐπ-αγγέλλω [in LXX: Est.4:8 (אָמַר), Pro.13:12, Wis.2:13, al. ;] __1. to announce, proclaim. __2. (a) to promise; __(b) to profess. Mid., also frequently in both these senses; __(with) to promise: with dab. of…

epanistemi.notes: ἐπ-αν-ίστημι [in LXX chiefly for קוּם ;] to raise up against; mid., to rise up against: before ἐπί, with accusative of person(s), Mat.10:21, Mrk.13:12.† (AS)

epanorthosis.notes: ἐπ-αν-όρθωσις, -εως, ἡ (ἐπανορθόω, to correct, restore; of. 2Ma.2:22) [in LXX: I Est.8:52, 1Ma.14:34 * ;] correction: of life, 2Ti.3:16 (cf. MM, Exp., xiv).† (AS)

epaphrizo.notes: ἐπ-αφρίζω to foam up: metaphorically, τ. αἰσχύνας, Ju 13.† (AS)

eparchia.notes: ἐπαρχεία (Rec. -χία, see Bl., § 3, 5), -ας, ἡ (ἔπαρχος, a prefect), [in LXX: Est.4:11 (מְדִינָה), Jdth.3:6 A* ;] the jurisdiction of a prefect, a province: Act.23:3, 34 25:1.† *†ἐπάρχεισς, -ον, of a prefect: ἡ ἐ.…

eparkeo.notes: ἐπ-αρκέω, -ῶ [in LXX: 1Ma.8:26 1Mac 11:35 * ;] __1. to be strong enough for. __2. to ward off. __3. to aid, relieve: with dative of person(s), 1Ti.5:10 5:16 (mid., WH, mg.).† (AS)

epathroizomai.notes: ἐπ-αθροίζω to assemble besides (Plut.): pass., Luk.11:29.† (AS)

epaulis.notes: ἔπ-αυλις, -εως, ἡ (αὐλή), [in LXX for חָצֵר, טִירָה, (l.with), etc. ;] a dwelling, habitation: Act.1:20 (LXX).† (AS)

epaurion.notes: ἐπ-αύριον, adv. [in LXX for מָחָר, Gen.30:33, elsewhere, Exo.9:6, al., for מׇחֳרָת ;] on the morrow: in NT, ἡ ἐ. (sc. ἡμέρα), Mat.27:62, Mrk.11:12, Jhn.1:29, Act.10:9, al (AS)

epautophoros.notes: αὐτόφωρος, -ον (αὐτός, φώρ, a thief) [in Sm.: Job.34:11 * ;] prop. with ref. to theft, then generally, in the very act: as freq., neut. dative after ἐπί, Jhn.8:4 (Rec., ἐπαυτοφώρῳ).† (AS)

epecho.notes: ἐπ-έχω [in LXX for חָדַל, etc.; also Sir.8:1 34:2, 2Ma.5:25 2Mac 9:25, al. ;] __1. to hold upon. __2. Like παρέχω (as in Hom., al.), to hold out, offer: λόγον ζωῆς, Php.2:16. __3. to hold or direct towards, Sc.νοῦν;…

epegeiro.notes: ἐπ-εγείρω [in LXX for עוּר hi., קוּם hi., etc. ;] to rouse up, excite: C. accusative of thing(s), διωγμόν, Act.13:50; ψυχάς, Act.14:2.† (AS)

epeidon.notes: ἐπ-εῖδον 2 aor. without Pres. in use; [in LXX chiefly for רָאָה ;] to regard with attention, look upon (in cl., of the gods) __1. with a view to bless: with inf., Luk.1:25 (cf. DB, 136b). __2. To punish: before ἐπί,…

epeisagoge.notes: ἐπ-εισ-αγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ a bringing in besides or in addition (Hipp., FlJ, al.): Heb.7:19 (cf. MM, Exp., xiv).† (AS)

epeita.notes: ἐπειτα, adv. of sequence [in LXX: Num.19:10 A, Isa.16:2, 4Ma.6:3 * ;] thereupon, thereafter, then: Luk.16:7, Gal.1:21, Jas.4:14; before μετὰ τοῦτο, Jhn.11:7; μετὰ ἔτη τρία, Gal.1:18; διὰ δεκατεσσάρων ἐτῶν, Gal.2:1;…

epekteinomai.notes: ἐπ-εκ-τείνω to extend: mid., to stretch forward: with dative, Php.3:13.† (AS)

ependuo.notes: ἐπ-εν-δύω = -δύνω (Hdt.), to put on over; pass. (Plut., al.), to have on over, be clothed upon: 2Co.5:2-4.† (AS)

ependutes.notes: ἐπενδύτης, -ου, ὁ (ἐπενδύω), [in LXX for מְעִיל Lev.8:7 A (Aq. ἐπένδυμα), 3Ki.18:4 A, 4Ki.13:18 * ;] an outer tunic (RV, coat): Jhn.21:7 .† (AS)

eperchomai.notes: ἐπ-έρχομαι, [in LXX for בּוֹא, עָבַר, etc. ;] __1. to come to, arrive, come on: before ἀπό, with genitive loc., Act.14:19 (ἐπῆλθαν; cf. M, Pr., 65; Deiss., BS, 191); of time, Eph.2:7. __2. to come upon (as in Hom.):…

epereazo.notes: ἐπηρεάζω (ἐπήρεια, spiteful abuse), to revile: with accusative of person(s), Luk.6:28; with accusative of thing(s) (but see ICC, in l), 1Pe.3:16.† (AS)

eperotao.notes: ἐπ-ερωτάω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for שָׁאַל, also for דָּרַשׁ, etc. ;] __1. to in­quire of, consult, question: with accusative of person(s), Mrk.12:34, Luk.2:46, al.; with dupl. accusative, Mrk.7:17 11:29, Luk.20:40,…

eperotema.notes: ἐπ-ερώτημα, -τος, τό [in LXX: Da TH Dan.4:14 (שְׁאֵלָא), Sir.33:3 * ;] __1. a question, au inquiry (Hdt., Thuc.). __2. a demand: 1Pe.3:21 (see ICC, in l).† (AS)

ephallomai.notes: ἐφάλλομαι [in LXX for צָלַח, 1Ki.10:6 11:6 16:13 * ;] to leap upon: before ἐπί with accusative of person(s) Act.19:16.† (AS)

ephapax.notes: ἐφ-άπαξ, adv. __1. once for all (Eupol.): Rom.6:10 Heb.7:27 9:12 10:10. __2. at once: 1Co.15:6.† (AS)

ephemeria.notes: ἐφ-ημερία, -ας, ἡ (ἐφήμερος), [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁמֶרֶת, מַחֲלֹקֶת ;] __1. a course of daily services (Neh.13:30, 1Ch.25:8, al.). __2. a class or course of priests detailed for service in the temple (1Ch.23:6,…

ephemeros.notes: ἐφ-ήμερος, -ον (ἐπί, ἡμέρα), __1. lasting for a day. __2. daily, for the day: Jas.2:15.† (AS)

ephesos.notes: Ἔφεσος, -ου, ἡ Ephesus, a city in Asia Minor Act.18:19, 21 18:24, 27 19:1, 17 19:26 (on the genitive, see M, Pr., 73) Act.20:16-17, 1Co.15:32 16:8, Eph.1:1, 1Ti.1:3, 2Ti.1:18 4:12, Rev.1:11 2:1.† (AS)

epheuretes.notes: ἐφ-ευρετής, -οῦ, ὁ (ἐφευρίσκω, to find out) an inventor, contriver: κακῶν (cf. κακίας εὑρετής, 2Ma.7:31), Rom.1:30.† (AS)

ephikneomai.notes: ἐφ-ικνέομαι, -οῦμαι [in LXX: Sir.43:27, 30 R (ἀφικ- ABא)* ;] to come to, to reach: before ἄχρι, 2Co.10:13; εἰς, 2Co.10:14.† (AS)

ephistemi.notes: ἐφ-ίστημι [in LXX for נָצַב ni., שִׁית, נָתַן, etc. ;] __1. causal in pres., impf., fut., 1 aor., to set upon or by, set up, etc. (Æsch., Hdt., Arist., al). __2. Intrans. in mid, and in pf. and 2 aor. act.; __(a) to…

ephphatha.notes: ἐφφαθά (Aram. אֶתְפְּתח, see Abbott, Essays, 142 ff.; DCG, i, 522) ephphatha, be opened: Mrk.7:34.† (AS)

ephraim.notes: Ἐφραίμ, (-ΐμ, Tr.) Ephraim, a town near Jerusalem: Jhn.11:54.† (AS)

epibaino.notes: ἐπι-βαίνω [in LXX chiefly for רָכַב ;] __1. to get up on, mount: before ἐπί, with accusative, Mat.21:5 (LXX); to embark in (a boat), go aboard: with dative, Act.27:2; before εἰς, Act.21:6 (Rec.); absol., Act.21:2.…

epiballo.notes: ἐπι-βάλλω [in LXX for שָׁלַח, שִׁית, etc. ;] __1. trans., to cast, lay or put upon: with accusative and dative, Mrk.11:7, 1Co.7:35; with accusative, before ἐπί with accusative, Rev.18:10, WH, mg.; τ. Χεῖρα (-ας) ἐπί…

epibareo.notes: ἐπι-βαρέω, -ῶ to put a burden on, be burdensome: figuratively, absol., 2Co.2:6; with accusative of person(s), 1Th.2:9, 2Th.3:8 (cf. M, Th., I, 29).† (AS)

epibibazo.notes: ἐπι-βιβάζω [in LXX chiefly for רָכַב hi. ;] to place upon: with accusative of person(s), Luk.10:34 19:35, Act.23:24.† (AS)

epiblema.notes: ἐπί-βλημα, -τος, τό [in LXX: Isa.3:22 * ;] __1. that which is thrown over, a cover. __2. a tapestry, hanging (Is, l.with). __3. that which is put on; __(a) embroidery; __(b) a patch: Mat.9:16, Mrk.2:21, Luk.5:36.† (AS)

epiblepo.notes: ἐπι-βλέπω [in LXX for נָבַט hi., פָּנָה, רָאָה, etc. ;] to look upon. In NT, as in LXX (1Ki.1:11 9:1, Psa.25:16; Tob.3:3, al.), to look on with favour: before ἐπί with accusative of person(s), Luk.1:48 9:38,…

epiboule.notes: ἐπι-βουλή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX: Est.2:22, I Est.5:73, 2Ma.5:7, al. ;] a plan against, a plot: Act.9:24 20:3, 19 23:30.† (AS)

epicheireo.notes: ἐπιχειρέω, -ῶ (χεῖρ), [in LXX for חָשַׁב, Exo.9:25; גָּמַל, 2Ch.20:11, al. ;] __1. to pat one's hand to. __2. to take in hand, attempt: with inf., Luk.1:1, Act.9:29 19:13.† (AS)

epicheo.notes: ἐπι-χέω [in LXX chiefly for יָצַק. Gen.28:18, al. ;] to pour upon: Luk.10:34.† (AS)

epichoregeo.notes: ἐπι-χορηγέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Sir.25:22, 2Ma.4:9 A * ;] to supply, provide: with accusative of thing(s), 2Pe.1:5; id. with dative of person(s), 2Co.9:10, Gal.3:5; pass., Col.2:19, 2Pe.1:11 (cf. χορηγέω, and see MM, Exp.,…

epichoregia.notes: ἐπι-χορηγία, -ας, ἡ (ἐπιχορηγέω), a supply: Eph.4:16, Php.1:19.† (AS)

epichrio.notes: ἐπι-χρίω [in Sm.: Eze.13:10 22:28 * ;] to spread on, anoint: with accusative, Jhn.9:11; id. before hi-I, with accusative, Jhn.9:6 (cf. MM, Exp., xiv).† (AS)

epidechomai.notes: ἐπι-δέχομαι [in LXX: Jdth.13:13 B2, 1Ma.10:1 1Mac 14:23, Sir.51:26, al. ;] __1. in cl., of things, to allow of, admit of (Dem., Arist., al.). In late writers, __2. to accept besides (Polyb.), to accept (in π. of the…

epideiknumi.notes: ἐπι-δείκνυμι [in LXX: Pro.12:17 (פּוּחַ hi.), Isa.37:26 (בּוֹא hi.), Esp. Jer.59, 2Ma.15:32, al ;] __1. to show, exhibit, display: with accusative and dative, Mat.16:1 22:19 24:1, Luk.17:14. Mid., to display for…

epidemeo.notes: ἐπι-δημέω, -ῶ (δῆμος); __1. to be at home (Thuc., Plat., al.), __2. to stay in a place, sojourn (Plat., Xen., al.; and see MM, Exp., xiv): Act.2:10 17:21; before ἐν, Act.18:27 (WH, mg.).† (AS)

epidiatassomai.notes: ἐπι-δια-τάσσομαι to add provisions to a document: Gal.3:15 (cf. ἐπιδιαθήκη, a second will, F1J, BJ, ii, 2, 3; the word is used of wills in π., cf. Deiss., LAE, 87).† (AS)

epididomi.notes: ἐπι-δίδωμι [in LXX for נָתַן, etc. ;] __1. to give over, to hand: with accusative of thing(s) and dative of person(s), Mat.7:9, 19, Luk.11:11-12 24:30, 42, Act.15:30; pass. with dative of person(s), Luk.4:17. __2. to…

epidiorthoo.notes: ἐπι-δι-ορθόω to set in order further: Tit.1:5 (Inscr.; Cremer, 8O8).† (AS)

epiduo.notes: ἐπι-δύω [in LXX: Deu.24:15, Jos.8:29, Jer.15:9 (בּוֹא)* ;] to go down, set (of the sun): Eph.4:26.† (AS)

epieikeia.notes: ἐπιεικία (Rec. -είκεια), -ας, ἡ (ἐπιεικής), [in LXX: Wis.2:19 12:18 Bar.2:27, from LXX Bar.4:24, TH (3:42), 2Ma.2:22 2Mac 10:4, 3Ma.3:15 3Mac 7:6 * ;] fairness, moderation, gentleness ("sweet reasonableness," Matthew…

epieikes.notes: ἐπιεικής, -ές (εἰκός, likely), [in LXX: Psa.86:5 (סַלָּח), Est.8:13 * ;] __1. seemly, fitting (Hom.). __2. equitable, fair, moderate: 1Ti.3:3, Tit.3:2, 1Pe.2:18, Jas.3:17; τὸ ἐ. (Thuc., i, 76), Php.4:5 (cf. Mayor,…

epigambreuo.notes: ἐπι-γαμβρεύω (γαμβρός, a connection by marriage) [in LXX: Gen.34:9, 1Ki.18:21 ff., 2Ch.18:1, Est.9:14 (חָתַן hithp.), Gen.38:8 R (יָבַם pi.), 1Ma.10:54-56 * ;] __1. to enter into affinity with: with dative (LXX, H.…

epigeios.notes: ἐπί-γειος, -ον (ἐπί, γῆ), of the earth, earthly: τὰ ἐ., Jhn.3:12 Php.2:10 3:19 (anarth.); σώματα, 1Co.15:40; οἰκία, 2Co.5:1; σοφία, Jas.3:15 (Cremer, 153).† (AS)

epiginomai.notes: ἐπι-γίνομαι (see: γίνομαι) [in LXX: Ep. Jer.47:1-7, 3Ma.2:6 * ;] to arrive, arise, come on: Act.28:13.† (AS)

epiginosko.notes: ἐπι-γινώσκω [in LXX chiefly for נָכַר: hi., also for יָדַע, etc. ;] "directive" of γινώσκω (AR, Eph., 249), as in cl.; __1. to observe, perceive, discern, recognize; __(a) absol.: Act.25:10, 1Co.13:12; before ὅτι,…

epignosis.notes: ἐπί-γνωσις, -εως, ἡ (ἐπιγινώσκω, which see), [in LXX: 3Ki.7:14 (B. γν-), Pro.2:5, Hos.4:1, 6 6:6 (דַּעַת), Jdth.9:14, 2Ma.9:11 * ;] acquaintance, discernment, recognition (Plut., al.): Php.1:9, Col.3:10; with…

epigraphe.notes: ἐπι-γραφή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἐπιγράφω), an inscription: Mat.22:20, Mrk.12:16 15:26, Luk.20:24 23:33.† (AS)

epigrapho.notes: ἐπι-γράφω [in LXX for כָּתַב, Num.17:2; fig., Jer.31:33, al. ;] to write upon, inscribe: Mrk.15:26, Act.17:23, Rev.21:12; figuratively, Heb.8:10 (LXX) Heb.10:16.† (AS)

epikaleo.notes: ἐπι-καλέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for קָרָא ;] __1. to call, name, surname: with accusative (cl.), Mat.10:25; pass., Act.1:23 4:36 10:5, 18 10:22 11:13 12:12, 25, Heb.11:16; τ. ὄνομα, before ἐπί (denoting possession, as…

epikalumma.notes: ἐπι-κάλυμμα, -τος, τό (ἐπικαλύπτω), [in LXX: Exo.26:14 39:34, (מְכַסֶּה), 4Ki.17:19 (מָסָךְ), Job.19:29 (aliter in Heb.)* ;] a cover, veil: metaphorically, τ. κακίας, 1Pe.2:16.† (AS)

epikalupto.notes: ἐπι-καλύπτω [in LXX for כָּסָה, etc. ;] to cover over, cover up: metaphorically, Rom.4:7 (LXX).† (AS)

epikataratos.notes: ἐπι-κατ-άρατος, -ον (ἐπικαταράομαι, to imprecate curses on), [in LXX for אָרַר, also Wis.3:12 14:8, 4Ma.2:19 ;] accursed: Gal.3:10 (LXX) Gal.3:13 (LXX κεκαταραμένος) (Cremer, 109).† (AS)

epikathizo.notes: ἐπι-καθ-ίζω [in LXX for רָכַב, etc. ;] to sit upon: Mat.21:7.† (AS)

epikeimai.notes: ἐπι-κείμαι [in LXX: Exo.39:31 (נָתַן), Job.19:3 (הָכַר hi.) Job.21:27 (חָמַס), 1Ma.6:57, 2Ma.1:21, 3Ma.1:22 * ;] to be placed, lie on: Jhn.21:9; before ἐπί, with dative, Jhn.11:38; figuratively, Heb.9:10; ἀνάγκη,…

epikoureios.notes: Ἐπικούριος (Rec. -ειος), -ου, ὁ an Epicurean, a follower of Epicurus: Act.17:18.† (AS)

epikouria.notes: ἐπικουρία, -ας, ἡ (ἐπικουρέω to be an ἐπίκουρος, an ally) [in LXX: Wis.13:18 * ;] aid, assistance: Act.26:22.† (AS)

epikrino.notes: ἐπι-κρίνω [in LXX: 2Ma.4:47, 3Ma.4:2 * ;] to decree, give sentence: with accusative and inf., Luk.23:24.† (AS)

epilambano.notes: ἐπι-λαμβάνω [in LXX for חָזַק hi., אָחַז, etc. ;] always mid. in LXX and NT (see Cremer, 758), to lap hold of: with genitive of person(s), Mat.14:31, Act.17:19 21:30, 33; with accusative of person(s) (not cl.),…

epilanthano.notes: ἐπι-λανθάνομαι (alternative mid, form of ἐπιλήθω, to cause to forget) [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכַח ;] to forget, neglect: with inf., Mat.16:5, Mrk.8:14; with genitive, Heb.6:10 13:2, 16; with accusative (as…

epilego.notes: ἐπι-λέγω [in LXX chiefly for בָּחַר ;] __1. to say in addition (Hdt.). __2. to call by name, to call: Jhn.5:2. __3. to choose; mid., to choose for oneself: Act.15:40.† (AS)

epileipo.notes: ἐπι-λείπω [in LXX: Ob 5 א1 R (שָׁאַר hi.) * ;] to fail: with accusative of person(s), Heb.11:32.† (AS)

epilesmone.notes: ἐπι-λησμονή, -ις, ή (επιλήθω), [in LXX: Sir.11:27 * ;] forgetful­ness: ἀκροατὴς ἐ. (genitive of qual.), Jas.1:25.† (AS)

epiloipos.notes: ἐπί-λοιπος, -ον (λοιπός), [in LXX for יָתַר, שָׁאַר ;] still left, remaining: χρόνος, 1Pe.4:2.† (AS)

epiluo.notes: ἐπι-λύω [in Aq.: Gen.40:8 41:8, 12; Th.: Hos.3:4 * ;] __1. to loose, release. __2. to solve, settle, explain: Mrk.4:34, Act.19:39.† (AS)

epilusis.notes: ἐπί-λυσις -εως, ἡ (ἐπιλύω), [in Aq.: Gen.40:8; Sm.: Hos.3:4 * ;] __1. release. __2. solution, interpretation: 2Pe.1:20.† (AS)

epimartureo.notes: ἐπι-μαρτυρέω, -ῶ to bear witness to: with accusative and inf., 1Pe.5:12,† (AS)

epimeleia.notes: ἐπιμέλεια, -ας, ἡ (ἐπιμελέομαι), [in LXX: Pro.3:8 (שִׁקּוּי), Wis.13:13, Est.6:10, 1Ma.16:14, al. ;] attention, care: Act.27:3 (see Field, Notes, 143).† (AS)
